With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order [MATH], where [MATH] is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to [MATH]. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to [MATH] and [MATH], respectively, where [MATH] describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.
tldr: This paper uses quantum mean estimation to improve convergence rates for gradient-based simulation optimization, establishing minimax-optimal query complexity exponents.
motivation: Classical gradient-based simulation optimization with noisy finite-difference gradients has convergence rates limited by query budget; the authors ask whether quantum mean estimation can improve these rates.
method: They apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences, progressively tighten estimation accuracy as perturbation sizes shrink, and analyze coupled evaluations plus matching lower bounds.
result: Quantum estimation improves the expected objective gap convergence exponent and, with coupling, halves the accuracy exponent relative to classical methods; matching lower bounds show minimax optimality for fixed decision dimension.
conclusion: Quantum mean estimation provides provable query-complexity advantages for convex simulation optimization, including feasible-query and boundary-optimum settings.

title: Scaling Limits Of Time-averaged Distributions For Symmetric Quantum Walks On Hypercubes
authors: Yusuke Ide, Norio Konno, Shuhei Mano
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube [MATH] associated with symmetric random walks, that is, random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on the Hamming distance, using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, we show that the time-averaged distribution of the Hamming distance is a discrete arcsine law whenever the eigenvalues are distinct. For discrete-time walks, exact formulas for the time-averaged distribution are known as combinatorial sums or as mixtures involving Krawtchouk polynomials, but their scaling limits as [MATH] (time average first) have not been specified. We obtain them explicitly for three random walks: the simple random walk (an arcsine law), the random walk with binomial weights (an equal mixture of arcsine laws with different supports), and the independent random walk (atoms of mass [MATH] at [MATH] and at [MATH]). Comparing with the continuous-time limits, the two models agree for the simple random walk but differ for the other two, so the correspondence between them is not universal.
tldr: The paper derives explicit scaling limits of time-averaged Hamming-distance distributions for continuous- and discrete-time quantum walks on hypercubes, showing arcsine laws and their mixtures.
motivation: Time-averaged distributions of quantum walks on hypercubes are known in combinatorial or Krawtchouk-polynomial form, but their scaling limits in the large-cube limit (with time averaging taken first) had not been explicitly characterized, and the relation between continuous- and discrete-time models was unclear.
method: Using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials, the authors analyze symmetric walks (transition probabilities depending only on Hamming distance), deriving discrete arcsine laws for continuous-time walks with distinct eigenvalues and exact combinatorial/Krawtchouk-mixture formulas for discrete-time walks before taking scaling limits.
result: Explicit limits are obtained for three walks: the simple random walk (arcsine law), binomial-weight walk (equal mixture of arcsine laws with different supports), and independent walk (atoms of mass at the endpoints). Continuous- and discrete-time limits agree only for the simple random walk.
conclusion: The correspondence between continuous- and discrete-time quantum-walk limits is not universal, and the limiting laws depend sensitively on the walk's symmetry structure.

title: Deterministic Polar Subcode Design Via Exact Low-Weight Spectrum Characterization
authors: Junhua You, Shaohua Wu, Aolin Liu, Yajing Deng, Qinyu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.32145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a deterministic framework for improving polar-subcode minimum distance through information-set selection and dynamic frozen expression design. Expression design faces two difficulties. Changing an expression can introduce new low-weight codewords, and excluding different codewords can impose conflicting requirements on the same coefficients. To address both difficulties, we first fix the information set and release the editable frozen constraints to form a common supercode containing every candidate code. Its low-weight codewords give necessary and sufficient conditions for one coefficient assignment to exclude every codeword of the specified weights. To apply these conditions at longer lengths, we use the polar decomposition. At each split, a one in the left codeword gives two complementary output bits whose combined weight is always one. We can therefore eliminate the corresponding variables from the parity checks and count their compatible assignments to obtain the exact low-weight spectrum. With both constituent codes fixed, the same reduced checks also simplify the coefficient search. Assignments that give identical check values across all relevant messages share one representative, from which the entire group can be recovered. We give sufficient conditions for choosing the coefficients sequentially without backtracking. Finally, we use the outcome of expression design on one information set to guide exchanges of information positions for the next, linking the two design steps. In experiments spanning block lengths from 64 to 1024 and several code rates, the proposed design meets the target minimum distances in minutes and achieves competitive frame error rates under successive cancellation list decoding.
tldr: The paper proposes a deterministic framework for designing polar subcodes with improved minimum distance via information-set selection and dynamic frozen expressions.
motivation: Polar subcodes can improve minimum distance and finite-length performance, but expression design is complicated by new low-weight codewords and conflicting coefficient constraints.
method: It fixes the information set, forms a common supercode, characterizes exact low-weight spectra using polar decomposition, and uses reduced parity checks to search frozen-expression coefficients and guide information-set exchanges.
result: Experiments for block lengths 64–1024 and several rates meet target minimum distances within minutes and achieve competitive frame error rates under SCL decoding.
conclusion: The deterministic low-weight-spectrum-based design links frozen-expression optimization with information-set selection and provides an efficient practical method for polar-subcode construction.

title: Ternary Perfect $2$-Burst-Correcting Codes
authors: Tuvi Etzion
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A construction for a ternary perfect linear [MATH]-burst-correcting code is presented for every redundancy [MATH]. The construction is recursive with seeds given for [MATH]. The construction of redundancy [MATH] is derived from a code of redundancy [MATH] and it distinguishes between codes of even and odd length.
tldr: The paper constructs ternary perfect linear 2-burst-correcting codes for every redundancy using a recursive method.
motivation: Perfect burst-correcting codes are a classical coding-theory topic concerned with correcting localized error bursts in storage and communication channels.
method: The author gives a recursive construction of ternary perfect linear 2-burst-correcting codes, with explicit seed codes for small redundancies and separate treatments for even and odd code lengths.
result: The construction yields ternary perfect linear 2-burst-correcting codes for every redundancy, extending known code families via recursion.
conclusion: The work advances classical coding theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On The Concentration Of The Ambiguity Function On Centered Balls
authors: Fabio Nicola
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the [MATH] concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.
tldr: The paper proves that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and unimodular constants.
motivation: The concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls is a fundamental question in time-frequency analysis, and a sharp characterization of extremizers is desirable.
method: The proof uses ideas from quantum information theory, likely relating the ambiguity function to phase-space representations and employing information-theoretic inequalities.
result: The Gaussian is shown to be the unique maximizer of the ambiguity-function concentration on any centered ball, modulo the natural symmetries.
conclusion: This establishes a sharp uncertainty-type principle for the ambiguity function and illustrates a fruitful connection between time-frequency analysis and quantum information theory.

title: Longitudinal-dither Wavefront Sensing: Calibration-free Measurement Of Mode Mismatch
authors: Masayuki Nakano
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mode mismatch between a gravitational-wave detector and the beams injected into it lowers the power stored in the arms and the level of squeezing. Correcting it requires the complex amplitudes of the three second-order modes, measured on a calibrated scale with the cavity on resonance at its operating power. Here we present a method that obtains a signal proportional to the mismatch by moving the beam on the wavefront sensors already used for alignment control. A longitudinal dither of the cavity adds to the resonant mode a reference field, which reaches the sensors through the same signal chains and so calibrates both the scale of this signal and the Gouy phases of the sensors and actuators, with no external calibration. We demonstrate the method on an optical cavity held on resonance in its operating state at input powers of 2 W and 62 W. At 2 W it yields an optical model that agrees with independent measurements in the mode content, and with the layout model in the actuator Gouy phase within its uncertainty of about [MATH]. At 62 W the thermally induced change of the eigenmode is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position changes. The method requires only components that every controlled cavity already possesses and enables continuous in situ monitoring of the mode matching in the operating state.
tldr: A calibration-free wavefront-sensing technique that measures mode mismatch between a squeezed-light/GW-detector beam and an optical cavity by longitudinally dithering the cavity to generate an in-situ reference field.
motivation: Mode mismatch between injected beams and the arm cavities of gravitational-wave detectors degrades stored power and squeezing levels, and correcting it normally requires externally calibrated measurements of the second-order mode amplitudes at operating power.
method: A longitudinal dither of the resonant cavity adds a reference sideband field that propagates through the same sensing chains as the mismatch signal, allowing simultaneous in-situ calibration of the signal scale and of the Gouy phases of sensors and actuators, using only hardware already present in controlled cavities.
result: Demonstrated on a resonant optical cavity at 2 W and 62 W input power: at 2 W the reconstructed optical model agrees with independent mode-content measurements and with the layout model for actuator Gouy phase; at 62 W the thermally induced eigenmode change is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position shifts.
conclusion: The method enables continuous, calibration-free monitoring of mode matching in the operating state of interferometric detectors, with potential benefits for maintaining squeezing and stored power in GW observatories.

title: Single-shot On-chip Measurement Of The Modal Stokes Parameters
authors: Amin Hashemi, Abbas Shiri, Bahaa E. A. Saleh, Andrea Blanco-Redondo, Ayman F. Abouraddy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated photonics has recently facilitated manipulating multimode partially coherent light in a compact mesh of Mach-Zehnder interferometers. A critical task in this context is on-chip reconstruction of the coherence matrix through a sequence of measurement configurations, thus giving rise to a speed bottleneck stemming from temporal delays in tuning on-chip phase shifts. Here we demonstrate single-shot reconstruction of the coherence matrix for two-mode partially coherent light by parallelizing the on-chip measurements of the modal Stokes parameters, thereby exchanging space for time. Although a larger chip area is required, the reconstruction is limited only by detection speed, thus potentially paving the way to real-time reconstruction of coherence matrices for applications in high-speed communications, cryptography, computation, and sensing.
tldr: The paper demonstrates single-shot on-chip reconstruction of the coherence matrix for two-mode partially coherent light by parallelizing measurements of modal Stokes parameters.
motivation: Integrated photonic platforms can manipulate multimode partially coherent light, but reconstructing the coherence matrix typically requires sequential tuning of on-chip phase shifts, creating a speed bottleneck.
method: The authors use a mesh of Mach-Zehnder interferometers to measure modal Stokes parameters in parallel, exchanging space for time and enabling single-shot reconstruction limited only by detection speed.
result: Single-shot reconstruction of the coherence matrix for two-mode partially coherent light is achieved on-chip, at the cost of larger chip area.
conclusion: This approach may enable real-time coherence-matrix reconstruction for high-speed communications, cryptography, computation, and sensing, though it is primarily an integrated photonics measurement technique rather than a quantum-information-theoretic contribution.

title: Upper And Lower Bounds For The Critical Point Of The Three-dimensional Ising Model
authors: Zhongpu Qiu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the critical point [MATH] of the nearest-neighbour Ising ferromagnet on [MATH] satisfies [MATH], equivalently [MATH], with both endpoints given by explicit rational numbers. To our knowledge these are the sharpest rigorous bounds available. They improve the classical bounds of Fisher (1967) and of Fr\"ohlich, Simon and Spencer (1976), narrowing the rigorously known interval by a factor of about 3.5, and the interval contains the numerical estimate of the critical point. For the lower bound we refine Fisher's self-avoiding-walk argument. A shortest path in the high-temperature expansion forbids all bonds spanned by its vertices, and the resulting gain is estimated through local correlation integrals and summed over paths by a finite-memory transfer bound. As a by-product, the connective constant of [MATH] is shown to be at most [MATH]. For the upper bound we prove an infrared bound whose coefficient involves the nearest-neighbour correlation. We keep the zero Fourier mode as an unknown and force it to be positive by exact local relations for the spins on a small shell. The finite inequalities entering the proof are verified in exact rational arithmetic, and the passage to the thermodynamic limit is proved analytically.
tldr: The paper rigorously narrows the interval containing the critical inverse temperature of the nearest-neighbour Ising ferromagnet on the three-dimensional cubic lattice, improving bounds of Fisher and of Fröhlich–Simon–Spencer by a factor of about 3.5.
motivation: Rigorous bounds on the 3D Ising critical point have remained far from the numerically estimated value since the classical results of the 1960s–70s, leaving a wide unproven gap around the phase transition.
method: The lower bound refines Fisher's self-avoiding-walk argument using high-temperature expansion path exclusions estimated via local correlation integrals and a finite-memory transfer bound (also yielding a bound on the lattice connective constant); the upper bound proves an infrared bound whose coefficient involves the nearest-neighbour correlation, treating the zero Fourier mode as an unknown constrained by exact local spin relations, with finite inequalities checked in exact rational arithmetic.
result: Explicit rational endpoints are obtained for the critical point, shrinking the rigorous interval by roughly a factor of 3.5 while still containing the numerical estimate, and the connective constant of the cubic lattice is bounded above.
conclusion: The work provides the sharpest known rigorous bounds on the 3D Ising critical temperature, a result in rigorous classical statistical mechanics rather than quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: QuOptLab: Advancing Quantum Optics Experiments With An Ai Agent
authors: Yuqing Li, Zeguan Wu, Yu Gan, Min Chen, Junyu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.32000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in AI-assisted theoretical research suggest that AI agents can contribute to research-level problems. Whether they can also advance experimental research by conducting experiments, analyzing the results, and proposing better experimental designs remains an open question. To address this question, we build a simulated quantum optics laboratory and integrate it with an AI agent in QuOptLab. The laboratory includes optical instruments, a robotic arm, and cameras, enabling the agent to carry out and iteratively refine experiments. We consider two complementary tasks: thin-film thickness measurement in free-space optics and edge-coupler design in integrated photonics. In the thin-film thickness measurement task, the agent repeatedly analyzes measurement results and revises its measurement method, including calibration and data analysis, reducing thickness-estimation error from 7.13 to 0.066~nm[MATH] over six epochs in a classical-interference run. For edge-coupler design, the agent iteratively proposes structural modifications, evaluates the resulting coupling performance, and uses the feedback to guide subsequent revisions, increasing simulated coupling efficiency from 85.81% to 91.98%.
tldr: QuOptLab integrates an AI agent with a simulated quantum optics laboratory to iteratively perform and improve two experimental tasks: thin-film thickness measurement and integrated-photonics edge-coupler design.
motivation: The authors ask whether AI agents can contribute not only to theoretical research but also to experimental quantum optics by conducting experiments, analyzing results, and proposing improved designs.
method: They build a simulated quantum optics lab containing optical instruments, a robotic arm, and cameras, and connect it to an AI agent that iteratively refines measurement and design strategies based on feedback.
result: In the thin-film measurement task, the agent reduced thickness-estimation error from 7.13 nm to 0.066 nm over six epochs, and in edge-coupler design it increased simulated coupling efficiency from 85.81% to 91.98%.
conclusion: The study suggests that AI agents can autonomously improve certain quantum-optics experimental workflows, though the work is limited to simulated laboratory tasks and does not address the researcher's core quantum-information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-systems interests.

title: A Causal Schr\"odinger-Newton Theory That Conserves Energy And Momentum
authors: Daisuke Miki, Yanbei Chen, Yiqiu Ma, Yubao Liu, Selim M. Shahriar
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper provides a theoretical justification for using the Causal-Conditional Schr\"odinger-Newton theory (CCSN) as a phenomenological model for classical gravity sourced by quantum matter. In CCSN, the gravitational field is driven not by expectation values in the global quantum state, but by conditional expectation values of the stress-energy tensor evaluated on local states determined by measurement records in the causal past. Because these local states are defined operationally from measurement records, the formulation is independent of any particular interpretation of quantum measurement while leading to unambiguous phenomenological dynamics. We apply this framework to a self-gravitating optomechanical system under continuous measurement and show that the resulting stochastic Schr\"odinger evolution, augmented by a classical gravitational field sourced by local conditional stress-energy expectations, can be made consistent with energy-momentum conservation by introducing a corrector tensor. The corrector restores the conservation law without altering the leading Newtonian predictions of CCSN, contributing only negligible post-Newtonian corrections in current experimental regimes. These results place CCSN on firmer theoretical footing and clarify its role as a viable phenomenological model for ongoing and future tests of classical gravity coupled to quantum matter.
tldr: The paper develops a causal-conditional Schrödinger-Newton framework for classical gravity sourced by quantum matter and restores energy-momentum conservation via a corrector tensor.
motivation: Schrödinger-Newton-type models provide phenomenological descriptions of classical gravity coupled to quantum matter, but their formulation and conservation laws require firmer theoretical grounding.
method: The authors formulate gravity as sourced by local conditional expectation values of the stress-energy tensor determined by measurement records in the causal past, and apply this to a continuously measured self-gravitating optomechanical system.
result: They show that the stochastic Schrödinger evolution can be made consistent with energy-momentum conservation by adding a corrector tensor that leaves leading Newtonian predictions unchanged and gives negligible post-Newtonian corrections in current experiments.
conclusion: The CCSN framework is placed on firmer theoretical footing as a viable phenomenological model for testing classical gravity coupled to quantum matter.

title: A Constraint-Preserving Preconditioned Quantum Solver For Heterogeneous Brinkman Flo
authors: Franz Franchetti Shreya Savadatti
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation can reduce the number of evaluations needed to estimate an average, but its advantage in PDE uncertainty quantification depends on the cost of each coherent solve. We study this problem for incompressible Brinkman flow through a porous material with spatially varying drag. We first express the velocity in divergence-free coordinates using a polar Riesz map, obtaining a positive-definite system that preserves incompressibility in the exact formulation. We then introduce a Sobolev--Riesz preconditioner and prove that the resulting condition number is bounded by [MATH], independently of the grid resolution. We construct block encodings and reversible-arithmetic circuits for this formulation and show how to estimate the mean kinetic energy without reconstructing the full velocity field. By accounting for both sampling and solver costs, we establish conditions under which the method has a gate-complexity advantage over single-level classical grid-resolving solvers. Numerical experiments verify the conditioning bound and the accuracy of the circuit components at the tested sizes. The complexity advantage is conditional on the stated input and discretization assumptions; no quantum-hardware runtime advantage is demonstrated.
tldr: The paper develops a constraint-preserving, preconditioned quantum linear-solver pipeline for heterogeneous Brinkman flow, embedding it in quantum amplitude estimation to estimate mean kinetic energy with a provable grid-independent condition number.
motivation: Quantum amplitude estimation can quadratically reduce sampling cost in PDE uncertainty quantification, but the end-to-end advantage hinges on the cost of each coherent linear solve, which the authors aim to control via better-conditioned formulations.
method: They rewrite the velocity in divergence-free coordinates using a polar Riesz map to obtain a positive-definite incompressibility-preserving system, add a Sobolev-Riesz preconditioner with a resolution-independent condition-number bound, and construct block encodings and reversible-arithmetic circuits for the resulting solver.
result: They derive conditions under which the method achieves a gate-complexity advantage over single-level classical grid-resolving solvers when both sampling and solver costs are counted, and numerical experiments confirm the conditioning bound and circuit-component accuracy at tested sizes.
conclusion: The quantum advantage is explicitly conditional on stated input and discretization assumptions, and no quantum-hardware runtime advantage is demonstrated.

title: Long-range Effective Interactions In A Rectangular Tight-binding Lattice Within The Semiclassical Approximation
authors: Diego Sanjines Evaristo Mamani
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the semiclassical formalism of Dunlap--Kenkre (1986) and of Mamani et al. (2017) to obtain the effective Hamiltonian of a rectangular tight-binding lattice with interactions to all neighbors, in the presence of a rapidly oscillating field [MATH] and a static potential [MATH], both arbitrary, by means of: a canonical transformation, the semiclassical approximation and the Kapitza-type time-averaging techniques (Mamani 2017). At zeroth order in [MATH], a field with even symmetry reparameterizes the hopping elements through factors in terms of Bessel functions. At order [MATH], the induced hopping elements arise from the coupling between the oscillating field and the curvature of the static potential (its 2nd derivative). For fields [MATH] with odd symmetry, in addition to renormalizing the interactions, an effective band shift appears. For the two-dimensional lattice, we obtain the generalization of the exact dynamic localization condition of Dignam et al. (2002) and Domachuk et al. (2002), and we show that the resulting band-collapse is in general anisotropic --axial interactions are suppressed but some diagonal interactions persist--, so that exact dynamic localization in the stroboscopic sense is guaranteed only when the band-collapse is complete for all neighbors. Finally, we numerically identify an effective-duplication scenario for the rectangular lattice, associated with approximate solutions of a Pythagorean-type relation among zeros of the zeroth-order Bessel function.
tldr: The paper develops a semiclassical effective-Hamiltonian formalism for a rectangular tight-binding lattice under arbitrary rapidly oscillating and static potentials, deriving renormalized and induced long-range hopping terms.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize Dunlap-Kenkre and related semiclassical averaging methods to rectangular lattices with all-neighbor interactions and to characterize dynamic localization and band-collapse conditions.
method: They use a canonical transformation, semiclassical approximation, and Kapitza-type time averaging to derive effective Hamiltonians up to first order in the inverse driving frequency.
result: At zeroth order, even-symmetry fields renormalize hopping via Bessel functions; at first order, induced hopping arises from coupling between the oscillating field and static-potential curvature, with odd-symmetry fields producing an effective band shift. For 2D rectangular lattices they find anisotropic band collapse and an effective-duplication scenario linked to a Pythagorean-type Bessel-zero relation.
conclusion: Exact stroboscopic dynamic localization in rectangular lattices requires complete band collapse across all neighbor directions, which is generally not achieved except under special conditions.

title: Electron Versus Positron Impact Ionization Of Inner Shells Of Heavy Atoms: Distortion, Exchange And Relativistic Effects
authors: Colm T. Whelan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triple differential cross sections are presented for electron and positron impact ionization of the K shells of Cu, Ag, Au and U and the L shells of Ag. Relativistic effects are important throughout. For positrons the recoil maximum is suppressed and the recoil-region spin asymmetry changes sign; for the [MATH] shell the binary peak changes. In symmetric geometry, where theory reproduces the measured absolute electron cross section, the positron peak lies on the other side of zero recoil. Measurements would test relativistic ionization theory in a regime that electron experiments cannot reach.
tldr: Relativistic distorted-wave calculations of triple differential cross sections for electron and positron impact ionization of K-shells of Cu, Ag, Au, U and L-shells of Ag, highlighting spin asymmetry and recoil/binary peak differences.
motivation: Positron impact ionization probes relativistic and exchange effects in a regime inaccessible to electron scattering experiments, providing a testbed for relativistic atomic collision theory.
method: Theoretical evaluation of triple differential cross sections using relativistic (Dirac) scattering treatments including distortion, exchange and relativistic corrections for K- and L-shell targets.
result: Positron impact suppresses the recoil maximum, reverses the sign of the recoil-region spin asymmetry, and alters the binary peak for the L shell; in symmetric geometry the positron peak appears on the opposite side of zero recoil.
conclusion: Proposed positron measurements would test relativistic ionization theory in a kinematic regime that electron experiments cannot reach.

title: Probing The Inner Structure Of Bound States
authors: Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, Karl Jansen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.
tldr: This paper uses quantum subspace expansion to construct composite-particle eigenstates in the massive Schwinger model and identify which operator classes are needed to capture their internal structure.
motivation: Understanding the internal structure of bound states in gauge theories is important, but standard eigenstate construction may obscure which operator sectors dominate. The authors aim to diagnose this by measuring fidelity contributions from different operator sets.
method: They apply quantum subspace expansion (QSE), optimizing states with different operator families and comparing their fidelities to the full QSE state. The scalar meson in the massive Schwinger model is used as a benchmark.
result: At large fermion mass, fermion bilinears suffice; at small mass, spatially extended meson-meson operators greatly improve fidelity, while short-distance four-fermion operators add little. The scalar charge and parton distribution function are sensitive to these operator choices.
conclusion: QSE is established as a tool for probing composite-particle structure and connecting operator content to observable properties, though the work is specialized to lattice gauge theory rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Colored Look At Anyons And Parastatistics
authors: Francesco Toppan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.
tldr: This paper reviews color Lie (super)algebras as a framework for describing parastatistics and anyonic braid statistics.
motivation: Color Lie (super)algebras, introduced by Rittenberg and Wyler, generalize ordinary Lie (super)algebras and have recently been connected to physical parastatistics. The author aims to update recent progress and promote a 'colored' perspective on particles beyond bosons and fermions.
method: The paper is a review/update of algebraic structures based on color Lie (super)algebras graded by abelian groups and defined via generalized Jacobi identities. It relates these structures to permutation-group paraparticles in arbitrary dimension and braid-group anyons in up to two spatial dimensions.
result: The color framework is argued to describe and provide physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics: permutation-exchanged paraparticles and braid-exchanged anyons.
conclusion: The work motivates further use of color Lie (super)algebras in parastatistics and braid statistics, but it is primarily a mathematical-physics review rather than a quantum-information result.

title: Single-Photon Detectors For Optical Wireless Communications: A Tutorial
authors: Ziyuan Shi, Yueying Zhan, Lei Yang, Mohamed-Slim Alouini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photon-counting receivers extend optical wireless communication (OWC) into regimes in which only a few detected photons are available per information bit, but the detector can no longer be treated as an interchangeable ideal counter. This tutorial develops a communication-oriented, port-to-bit framework for single-photon detection in indoor, terrestrial, airborne, space, underwater, non-line-of-sight, and integrated communication-and-sensing links. It compares SPADs, silicon photomultipliers, CMOS SPAD arrays, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, PMT/MCP-PMT receivers, upconversion detectors, and emerging technologies through photon-detection efficiency, timing, active area, dynamic range, spectral coverage, readout, cooling, and integration requirements. Beginning with the ideal Poisson channel, the tutorial then develops communication-level models for dead time, recovery, finite-pixel occupancy, saturation, background counts, afterpulsing, crosstalk, nonuniformity, and event loss. These models are connected to modulation, likelihood-based detection, synchronization, channel estimation, soft decoding, and detector-aware receiver processing, with numerical studies that compare algorithms under a common detector and detectors under a common algorithm. Finally, a unified link-budget and system co-design methodology is used to relate photons per bit, sensitivity, bandwidth, data rate, and link margin, and representative demonstrations are normalized to expose practical tradeoffs. The central conclusion is that useful photon efficiency is an end-to-end property of the optical front end, detector, readout, and digital receiver, rather than a detector metric in isolation.
tldr: This tutorial reviews single-photon detectors and communication-oriented models for photon-counting optical wireless communication links.
motivation: Photon-counting receivers enable optical wireless communication in few-photon-per-bit regimes, but real detectors introduce non-idealities that require communication-level modeling.
method: The authors survey SPADs, SiPMs, CMOS SPAD arrays, SNSPDs, PMT/MCP-PMTs, upconversion detectors, and emerging technologies, then develop models for dead time, saturation, background counts, afterpulsing, crosstalk, and related effects and connect them to modulation, detection, synchronization, and decoding.
result: Numerical studies compare algorithms under common detectors and detectors under common algorithms, and a unified link-budget methodology relates photons per bit, sensitivity, bandwidth, data rate, and link margin.
conclusion: Useful photon efficiency is an end-to-end property of the optical front end, detector, readout, and digital receiver rather than a detector metric in isolation.

title: An Equivariant Index Theorem For The Heisenberg Calculus
authors: Erik van Erp Alexander Gorokhovsky
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".
tldr: The paper proves a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds with a compact Lie group action.
motivation: Equivariant index theory for Heisenberg (contact) calculi lacks a local geometric formula analogous to the Atiyah–Segal–Singer fixed-point theorem for classical elliptic operators.
method: The authors construct traces on each fixed-point set via integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group, and reduce the problem K-theoretically to their earlier equivariant index theorem for Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds.
result: The equivariant index character is expressed as a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol, integrated over fixed-point data.
conclusion: The work extends equivariant index theory to the Heisenberg calculus, providing a local fixed-point formula and new trace constructions on contact manifolds.

title: Multiplicities And $k$-numerical Range
authors: Pan Shun Lau, Nancy de Menzelthe, Tin-Yau Tam
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the wedge and projection multiplicities of a point in the [MATH]-numerical range [MATH] of a complex matrix [MATH]. The representatives are decomposable wedges of orthonormal [MATH]-frames and rank-[MATH] orthogonal projections, respectively. For [MATH], put [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH]. We prove that every [MATH] satisfies [MATH] and [MATH]. We determine both multiplicities at every boundary point of [MATH], including non-exposed points. For complex symmetric matrices we establish lower bounds for both real multiplicities, including singular interior fibers, and obtain exact formulas for boundary points, line ranges, and commuting symmetric parts. We also relate the two multiplicities by quadratic inequalities.
tldr: The paper studies multiplicities of points in the k-numerical range of complex matrices using decomposable wedges and rank-k orthogonal projections.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the geometric and algebraic structure of the k-numerical range by analyzing the multiplicity of its points, including boundary and non-exposed points.
method: They represent points via orthonormal k-frames and rank-k projections, prove inequalities relating wedge and projection multiplicities, and derive exact multiplicity formulas for complex symmetric matrices.
result: The paper determines boundary multiplicities, establishes lower bounds for real multiplicities including singular interior fibers, and relates the two multiplicities through quadratic inequalities.
conclusion: The work contributes to matrix analysis and numerical range theory but has no direct connection to the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems research directions.

title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization For Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular And Wiretap Coding
authors: Bastian Loss, Ahmad Nimr, Gerhard Fettweis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.
tldr: The paper proposes a multi-user linear precoding framework for obfuscation-aided mixed regular and wiretap coding in classical physical-layer security.
motivation: Wiretap coding can secure communication via channel advantage but may severely reduce achievable rate under unfavorable channel conditions; mixed coding uses wiretap coding only for a short secret while regular coding carries the obfuscated payload.
method: The authors generalize an obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system using multi-user linear precoding, formulate a precoder optimization problem with a minimum secrecy-rate constraint abstracting the obfuscation function, and evaluate it via numerical simulations in a geometric two-user LoS channel.
result: Simulations show that the minimum secrecy-rate requirement determines the operating point between regular and wiretap coding, mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers, and sum-rate gains are largest when users are at similar angles.
conclusion: Mixed coding combined with linear precoding offers a flexible physical-layer security design, but the work is classical communication engineering and does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Supersymmetry Of Helmholtz Waves
authors: A. Dom\'inguez-Cruz, G. Badu, B. Perez-Garcia, B. M. Rodr\'iguez-Lara
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry organizes physical laws, links conservation principles to transformations, and reveals connections between seemingly different systems. We show that Helmholtz waves support Witten supersymmetry through their spatial symmetries, without additional internal degrees of freedom. Reflection across the transverse horizontal axis induces a [MATH] grading of the Euclidean algebra, whose odd generators supply charges connecting opposite-parity Cartesian and Bessel modes at equal separation eigenvalues. The Bessel model has an unpaired even zero mode, Witten index one, and unbroken supersymmetry for any rotation-axis position along the reflection line. We express all four separators through mixed supercommutators of displaced orbital-angular-momentum generators, establish Weber pairing through a spectral sign operator, and identify the obstruction to equal-eigenvalue Mathieu pairing at nonzero ellipticity. We extend our construction to multiple transverse shells and generate supersymmetric partner fields with a common Talbot recurrence. Gaussian apodization centered on the rotation axis gives finite-power fields and preserves our charge relations during exact forward propagation while modifying the ideal revival. Our framework may guide optical transformations between parity partners and the characterization of structured fields.
tldr: The paper shows that Helmholtz waves possess Witten supersymmetry through spatial reflection symmetries, connecting Cartesian, Bessel, Weber, and Mathieu mode families via supersymmetric partner fields.
motivation: The authors aim to reveal hidden supersymmetric structure in classical Helmholtz wave solutions without introducing internal degrees of freedom, using spatial symmetries and parity grading.
method: They construct a Z2 grading of the Euclidean algebra from reflection across a transverse axis, identify odd generators as supercharges linking opposite-parity modes, and express separators through mixed supercommutators of displaced orbital-angular-momentum generators.
result: The Bessel model exhibits an unpaired even zero mode, Witten index one, and unbroken supersymmetry for any rotation-axis position; Weber pairing is established via a spectral sign operator, and an obstruction to equal-eigenvalue Mathieu pairing at nonzero ellipticity is identified.
conclusion: The framework may guide optical transformations between parity partners and characterization of structured fields, with extensions to multiple transverse shells and supersymmetric partner fields sharing a common Talbot recurrence.

title: Phase Matching Of High-order Harmonics Driven By A Combined Coherent And Bright Squeezed Vacuum Field
authors: Yaoshun Sun, Shang Ma, Xintong He, Jiaao Cai, Wentao Wang, Mingxuan Li, Xiangyu Tang, Sizuo Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) driven by non-classical light provides new insights into light-matter interactions and paves the way to quantum attosecond spectroscopy. Achieving phase matching is vital for generating bright HHG sources, while it has received comparatively limited attention in quantum-light-driven HHG. In this work, we investigate the phase matching of HHG driven by an intense coherent field combined with a weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) field, using a semiclassical ensemble of coherent-field realizations sampled from the Husimi-[MATH] probability distribution. We reveal the physical mechanism behind the distinct pressure dependence of the harmonic yields for odd, even and half-integer sidebands spectral components, as observed in our previous experiment [arXiv:2607.20941]. The simulations and phase-matching model demonstrate that the BSV-induced perturbation of the electron action phase could introduce an additional sub-cycle phase mismatch, such that the amplitude of sub-cycle bursts could be significantly modified by gas pressure after macroscopic propagation, even when the harmonic yield is near the optimum. The resulting amplitude asymmetry of sub-cycle bursts leads to a significant intensity contrast between half-integer sidebands harmonics, manifesting as distinct pressure dependence of their yields. Our findings reveal the phase-matching mechanism in two-color quantum-light-driven HHG, and suggest opportunities for macroscopic control of the non-classical HHG source.
tldr: The paper studies phase matching in high-order harmonic generation driven by a combined coherent field and weak bright squeezed vacuum, explaining pressure-dependent sideband yields via a sub-cycle phase mismatch.
motivation: Non-classical light-driven high-order harmonic generation could enable quantum attosecond spectroscopy, but phase matching in such quantum-light-driven HHG has received limited attention.
method: The authors use a semiclassical ensemble of coherent-field realizations sampled from the Husimi probability distribution and develop a phase-matching model for the two-color quantum-light-driven HHG process.
result: The simulations show that the bright squeezed vacuum perturbs the electron action phase, introducing an additional sub-cycle phase mismatch that modifies sub-cycle burst amplitudes and produces distinct pressure dependence for odd, even, and half-integer sidebands.
conclusion: The work clarifies the phase-matching mechanism in two-color quantum-light-driven HHG and suggests routes for macroscopic control of non-classical HHG sources.

title: Mechanisms Of Turnkey Soliton Generation In Self-injection-locked Photonic-crystal Ring Resonators
authors: Naoya Kuse
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turnkey generation of dissipative Kerr solitons in photonic-crystal ring resonators relies on the interplay between engineered mode splitting, self-injection locking, and modulation instability, yet the mechanism governing soliton initiation and number selection remains incompletely understood. We investigate this interplay using coupled Lugiato-Lefever equations with a self-consistent nonlinear self-injection-locking condition. Analysis of continuous-wave steady states and their locking stability reveals operating points accessible through feedback-induced transitions between split resonances. Evaluating modulation-instability gain at these points identifies conditions for comb initiation and links the dominant unstable sideband modes to soliton-number selectivity. Direct time-domain simulations corroborate the analysis, showing that appropriately chosen mode splitting enables highly repeatable single-soliton generation without external laser-frequency scans. The final soliton number is nevertheless shaped by subsequent nonlinear evolution and feedback-induced detuning changes, rather than by the initial instability alone. We also show that larger dispersion suppresses higher-order unstable modes and favors lower soliton numbers.
tldr: The paper analyzes turnkey dissipative Kerr soliton generation in photonic-crystal ring resonators using coupled Lugiato-Lefever equations with self-injection locking.
motivation: Turnkey soliton initiation and soliton-number selection in photonic-crystal ring resonators are not fully understood, limiting repeatable comb generation without external laser scans.
method: The authors model continuous-wave steady states and locking stability under a self-consistent nonlinear self-injection-locking condition, then evaluate modulation-instability gain and corroborate with time-domain simulations.
result: Engineered mode splitting enables feedback-accessible operating points and repeatable single-soliton generation, while final soliton number is shaped by subsequent nonlinear evolution and feedback-induced detuning changes.
conclusion: Appropriate mode splitting and larger dispersion can favor lower soliton numbers and suppress higher-order unstable modes, clarifying mechanisms for turnkey soliton generation.

title: Encrypted Fixed-Point Multiplication In Quasilinear Complexity
authors: Junho Lee Jung Hee Cheon
abstract: ArXiv:2611.32157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Homomorphic encryption enables computation on encrypted data, but its high computational overhead remains a central obstacle. We overcome this obstacle asymptotically for high-precision fixed-point arithmetic. In this paper, we introduce focused encoding, which represents a fixed-point number of [MATH]-bit precision using a polynomial of degree [MATH] over a polynomially bounded modulus by concentrating precision at one embedding. We then introduce an error-shaping technique for homomorphic operations to preserve the encoding. This yields an encrypted fixed-point multiplication algorithm for the CKKS scheme that runs in online time [MATH] at [MATH]-bit precision for any fixed multiplicative depth, with security parameter [MATH]. Further, we develop bootstrapping for focused encoding to overcome the quadratic cost of conventional bootstrapping. We bootstrap ciphertext coefficients at an enlarged scale and shape the resulting error to preserve focused encoding, at the cost of additional modulus consumption. Then, to reduce the remaining logarithmic overhead, we decompose the ciphertext into components over a smaller subring and bootstrap each separately. This reduces the online cost per multiplication, including bootstrapping, to [MATH] for security parameter [MATH].
tldr: The paper introduces a 'focused encoding' and error-shaping technique that reduces the online cost of high-precision encrypted fixed-point multiplication in the CKKS homomorphic encryption scheme to quasilinear complexity, including a new bootstrapping procedure.
motivation: Homomorphic encryption allows computation on encrypted data, but its computational overhead is a central practical obstacle, especially for high-precision fixed-point arithmetic.
method: Fixed-point numbers of n-bit precision are encoded into degree-O(n) polynomials over a polynomially bounded modulus by concentrating precision at a single embedding, with an error-shaping technique to preserve the encoding through homomorphic operations; bootstrapping is adapted to this encoding by bootstrapping coefficients at enlarged scale and decomposing the ciphertext over a smaller subring.
result: The resulting encrypted multiplication algorithm runs in online time Õ(n) at n-bit precision for any fixed multiplicative depth, and including bootstrapping the online cost per multiplication is reduced to Õ(n) for security parameter λ.
conclusion: The work asymptotically overcomes the overhead bottleneck of CKKS for high-precision fixed-point arithmetic, though it remains a classical cryptographic/complexity contribution with no quantum information component.

title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear To Emergent And Solitonic Approaches
authors: Niko Brimi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This thesis investigates the role of nonlinearity in approaches beyond standard quantum mechanics, following a path from modifications of quantum dynamics to the possibility of an emergent statistical description. We first examine Weinberg's nonlinear formulation and its implications for the statistical interpretation of quantum states. We then discuss de Broglie-Bohm theory and the Madelung formulation, which provide a framework for comparing guided trajectories with ensemble descriptions involving momentum fluctuations. The Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach identifies the fluctuation energy associated with the quantum potential. We then investigate whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean formulation of the complex sine-Gordon model. Within a weak-noise approximation, we identify a regime in which the statistics of the soliton centres reproduce the Schr{\"o}dinger equation, with an effective action scale determined by the background fluctuations. This correspondence is established for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic. These results provide a concrete setting for exploring how quantum dynamics can emerge as a statistical description of underlying nonlinear field dynamics.
tldr: This thesis explores nonlinear modifications and emergent statistical descriptions of quantum mechanics, including soliton-based derivations of the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: The work is motivated by foundational questions about whether quantum dynamics can arise from deeper nonlinear or statistical field dynamics beyond standard quantum mechanics.
method: It analyzes Weinberg's nonlinear formulation, de Broglie-Bohm theory, the Madelung formulation, Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty, and a Galilean complex sine-Gordon soliton model under weak-noise approximations.
result: Within a weak-noise regime, the statistics of soliton centres reproduce the Schrödinger equation for Gaussian ensembles and at-most-quadratic potentials, with an effective action scale set by background fluctuations.
conclusion: The thesis provides a concrete setting for exploring emergent quantum dynamics from nonlinear field statistics, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: What Time Is It In Assembly Space? Cronin And Walker's "The Physics Of Causation" Fails Elementary Dimensional Analysis (Comment On arXiv:2601.00515)
authors: Philip Moriarty
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cronin and Walker claim that causation is quantified by an ``assembly index'', a count of the steps needed to build an object. Remarkably, they equate ``continuous time (as measured by clocks)'' to a multiple of the index, which is a dimensionless number. Their argument treats one parameter as simultaneously a rate, a time interval, and a pure number, and provides no timescale to convert index to clock time. This dimensional incoherence betrays, at best, an ill-conceived and ill-formed theory, and fatally undermines two central claims. First, the exponential weighting at the heart of what they call the assembly equation can be obtained only by supplying a timescale, which they never do, or by recasting clock time as a dimensionless count of assembly steps. In the latter case, their ``derivation'' trivially reduces to Bernoulli's seventeenth-century compound-interest limit. Second, lacking rates or energy scales, their account cannot predict how quickly, or under what conditions, anything forms, and yet formation ``in finite time'' is their criterion for distinguishing spontaneous from ``selected'' objects. Assembly theory is thus incapable of addressing causation.
tldr: A critical comment arguing that Cronin and Walker's assembly theory of causation fails elementary dimensional analysis, conflating a dimensionless assembly index with clock time.
motivation: Cronin and Walker claim causation can be quantified via an 'assembly index' and equate continuous clock time to a multiple of this dimensionless count; the author aims to show this is dimensionally incoherent.
method: Conceptual and dimensional-analysis critique of the assembly equation, examining the units of the exponential weighting and the missing timescale needed to convert index into physical time.
result: The claimed derivation either requires an unspecified timescale or collapses into Bernoulli's compound-interest limit when clock time is recast as a dimensionless step count; without rates or energy scales the theory cannot predict formation times.
conclusion: Assembly theory as presented cannot address causation, and its central claims about distinguishing spontaneous from selected objects are undermined.

title: Localization In One-dimensional Magnetic Quasicrystals
authors: Andrew Osborne, Rhine Samajdar, Andrew A. Houck
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The celebrated Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.
tldr: The paper studies localization and transport in one-dimensional quasiperiodic lattices whose graph topology and magnetic interference produce critical, exponential, or flat-band localization, including interaction effects.
motivation: The Aubry-André-Harper model provides a canonical setting for quasiperiodic localization, but the role of underlying graph topology and magnetic interference in mediating conducting-insulating competition is less explored.
method: The authors construct one-dimensional quasiperiodic lattice models with graph-mediated hopping and analyze single-particle eigenstates, mobility edges, and flat bands, then use exact diagonalization of bosonic dynamics to study interaction effects.
result: They find models with critically localized dispersive states, exponentially localized states, coexisting flat bands of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates, and exactly solvable mobility edges arising from graph structure; interactions drive localized states toward extendedness.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding how magnetic interference, graph topology, and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

title: From Growth Inhibition To Fluctuations: Testing An Ising Model Of Bacterial Responses To Antibiotics
authors: Pietro Cicuta, Morten Kals, Nir S. Gov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH). While both models describe the mean growth-rate dependence on antibiotic concentration comparably well, we find that the Ising model provides a markedly better description of PGRH, offering an additional and more stringent test of the collective description. The fitted Ising interaction strength is systematically related to the Hill exponent and increases with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from the protein-production machinery. These results provide experimental support for describing complex biochemical reaction networks through effective cooperative Ising interactions, and suggest that the collective response of bacterial growth to antibiotics reflects the organization of the underlying metabolic network.
tldr: The authors test whether an effective Ising model can describe bacterial growth-rate responses to antibiotics, comparing it with Hill-model fits for mean growth rate and population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH).
motivation: Complex biochemical reaction networks are often claimed to show emergent cooperativity capturable by few-parameter effective Ising models, but such mappings are rarely tested experimentally against standard phenomenological descriptions.
method: Three bacterial species were exposed to a range of antibiotics targeting different cellular functions; mean growth-rate dose responses and PGRH were fitted with both an effective Ising model and the conventional Hill model.
result: Both models fit the mean growth rate comparably, but the Ising model describes PGRH markedly better; the fitted Ising interaction strength tracks the Hill exponent and grows with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from protein production machinery.
conclusion: The data support effective cooperative Ising descriptions of biochemical networks and suggest that collective growth responses to antibiotics reflect the organization of the underlying metabolic network.

title: Temporal Soliton Waves In Modern Fiber Laser Systems
authors: Boris Malomed Shilong Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of temporal soliton-wave in modern fiber systems. Temporal soliton waves constitute a broad class of nonlinear localized structures in modern fiber laser systems, arising from different balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, spectral filtering, and various forms of cavity coupling. We review the underlying theory, basic experimental findings, and practical methods for the generation, real-time characterization, and active control of soliton families, with a particular focus on recent progress reported for mode-locked fiber-laser platforms. The families covered in the chapter include dissipative solitons, soliton molecules (bound states), and dispersion-managed solitons. For each species, we focus on the pulse energy, duration, stationary and breathing states, and emerging intelligent (machine-learning-assisted) control strategies.
tldr: This chapter reviews temporal soliton waves in mode-locked fiber laser systems, covering theory, experiments, characterization, and control.
motivation: Temporal solitons are important nonlinear localized structures in fiber lasers arising from balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, filtering, and cavity coupling.
method: The authors survey existing theoretical and experimental work on dissipative solitons, soliton molecules, and dispersion-managed solitons, including real-time characterization and machine-learning-assisted control.
result: The review organizes soliton families by pulse energy, duration, stationary and breathing states, and discusses recent progress in intelligent control strategies.
conclusion: The chapter provides a comprehensive reference on classical fiber-laser soliton dynamics, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cantor Spectrum At A Fixed Diophantine Frequency
authors: Rui Han, Wilhelm Schlag, Fan Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish that the spectrum of one-frequency analytic quasiperiodic Schrodinger operators exhibits Cantor structure in the regime of positive Lyapunov exponents for every fixed Diophantine frequency. The proof follows the general strategy of the gap construction by Goldstein and the second author, but avoids the elimination of double and triple resonances used in the original argument. A novel ingredient is the use of Holder continuity of the integrated density of states (IDS) to exclude energies at which eigenvalue parametrizations in finite volume have small slopes. We also use a linear bound in the volume on the number of zeros of Dirichlet determinants, and a pigeonholing argument to obtain lower bounds on the distances between eigenvalues. The crossing of two translated Rellich functions with opposite slopes produces a local maximum whose eigenfunctions have exponentially small boundary values. Together with finite volume eigenvalue separation, this forces the DOS mass to concentrate near the maximum. However, on an interval of constancy of the acceleration, the Lyapunov exponent is analytic, and hence the DOS is Lipschitz there. This ultimately leads to a contradiction near the maximum.
tldr: The paper proves Cantor spectrum for one-frequency analytic quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators at any fixed Diophantine frequency in the positive Lyapunov exponent regime.
motivation: Understanding the spectral structure of quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators is a central problem in mathematical physics, particularly whether the spectrum is Cantor-like under Diophantine conditions.
method: The authors adapt the Goldstein–Schlag gap construction, avoid elimination of double and triple resonances, and use Hölder continuity of the integrated density of states, bounds on zeros of Dirichlet determinants, and a pigeonholing argument to control eigenvalue separation.
result: They establish Cantor spectrum for every fixed Diophantine frequency in the positive Lyapunov exponent regime by deriving a contradiction from DOS concentration near a local maximum of translated Rellich functions.
conclusion: The work advances the mathematical theory of quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, And A Moduli-Space Route From Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
authors: Ji Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.
tldr: The paper studies 1+1-dimensional scalar field models with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, deriving exact tanh kinks, a sextic potential, and fluctuation spectra, and connects them to self-dual Yang-Mills via a moduli-space route.
motivation: Self-dual Yang-Mills theory is a generator of integrable equations, and the authors ask which potentials make prescribed kink solutions exact in models with nontrivial kinetic structure, and how such models could arise from gauge-theory moduli dynamics.
method: Euler-Lagrange and traveling-wave reduction with a first integral are used to solve the inverse problem for a quadratic spatial kinetic deformation; a Bogomolny-type formulation, vacuum curvature relations, admissibility analysis, and numerical fluctuation spectra establish stability, while a moduli-space expansion of BPS monopole/dyon dynamics motivates the kinetic terms.
result: A closed-form kink energy independent of the odd parameter, a sextic potential, positivity conditions controlling hyperbolicity and vacuum masses, and an exactly solvable fluctuation operator with a translation zero mode and no negative modes in the admissible region are obtained; the Taub-NUT metric provides an explicit realization.
conclusion: The deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact SDYM reduction, so the correct bridge is the moduli-space route; full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains an open research program.

title: Predictive Self-Entropy In Dirichlet Universal Coding: A Factor-Two Central Limit Theorem And A Markov Extension
authors: Thomas Sch\"urmann
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential universal coders produce both a realized log-loss and, before each symbol is observed, a predictive distribution with its own Shannon entropy. We compare the realized arithmetic code length with the cumulative predictive self-entropy, the prequential sum of the self-expected logarithmic scores of the issued forecasts. This forecast-only quantity is neither a plug-in entropy estimate nor a posterior entropy functional. For finite-alphabet memoryless sources and Dirichlet (add-[MATH]) sequential predictors, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the two normalized quantities. They have the same first-order entropy limit but different second-order fluctuations: for every nonuniform i.i.d. source, cumulative predictive self-entropy has exactly twice the leading asymptotic variance of realized code length, and the ordinary mean-square-error ratio converges to two. We also give its logarithmic bias coefficient. For fixed finite-order Markov sources with context-wise Dirichlet predictors, the factor-two result becomes a context/innovation covariance decomposition, recovering the i.i.d. factor two when only the innovation component contributes.
tldr: The paper proves a joint central limit theorem comparing cumulative predictive self-entropy with realized arithmetic code length for Dirichlet universal coding, including a factor-two variance result and a Markov extension.
motivation: Sequential universal coders issue predictive distributions whose self-entropy is a forecast-only quantity distinct from plug-in or posterior entropy estimates; the paper aims to characterize its asymptotic fluctuations relative to realized code length.
method: For finite-alphabet memoryless sources and Dirichlet sequential predictors, the author establishes a joint CLT for normalized cumulative predictive self-entropy and realized code length, then extends the analysis to finite-order Markov sources with context-wise Dirichlet predictors.
result: Both quantities share the same first-order entropy limit, but cumulative predictive self-entropy has exactly twice the leading asymptotic variance of realized code length for every nonuniform i.i.d. source; the Markov case yields a context/innovation covariance decomposition recovering the i.i.d. factor two when only the innovation component contributes.
conclusion: The work identifies a factor-two central limit phenomenon for prequential forecast entropy in Dirichlet universal coding and clarifies its distinction from standard entropy estimators.

title: Fuzzy Vectors From First And Second Moments: Affine Consistency, Carrying And Sparsest Realizations
authors: Paul Schneider Jan Schneider
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When the probability law of a random vector cannot be identified, its mean and possibly singular covariance can often still be elicited. We consider fuzzy vectors with compact convex cuts as mathematically tractable representations of such a moment pair, and ask how they must be designed to rely only on this information. We postulate two modeling desiderata, independence of the choice of origin and basis, and invariance under embeddings into a higher-dimensional space. Under these requirements alone we show that, in every ambient dimension, every level set of the fuzzy vector must be a Mahalanobis ellipsoid centered at the mean. Its complete specification then amounts to the choice of a radial profile for each covariance rank. We call a fuzzy vector a carrier of the moment pair if at least one of its random-set selections has exactly the given mean and covariance. For an ellipsoidal fuzzy vector of rank [MATH] with radial profile [MATH], carrying is equivalent to [MATH], and equality characterizes the inclusion-minimal carriers within the fixed-shape Mahalanobis class. A discrete random vector with the same mean and covariance and the fewest equally weighted atoms has its atoms on a regular simplex in Mahalanobis coordinates. Completing this simplex under the rotations left free by the moments yields the minimum-volume crisp ellipsoid in the state space that carries them. The ellipsoidal representation also encodes interaction through the covariance matrix.
tldr: This paper develops a mathematical framework for representing uncertain random vectors using fuzzy vectors constrained only by mean and covariance, deriving affine-consistent Mahalanobis ellipsoidal level sets and minimal simplex-based realizations.
motivation: When a random vector's full probability law is unknown but its mean and possibly singular covariance can be elicited, a tractable representation is needed that depends only on this moment information and respects invariance under coordinate choices and embeddings.
method: The authors impose origin/basis independence and embedding invariance, prove level sets must be Mahalanobis ellipsoids centered at the mean, characterize carrying of the moment pair via radial profiles, and construct sparsest equally weighted discrete realizations on regular simplices in Mahalanobis coordinates.
result: Carrying is equivalent to a condition on the radial profile, equality characterizes inclusion-minimal carriers within the fixed-shape Mahalanobis class, and completing the simplex under free rotations yields the minimum-volume crisp ellipsoid carrying the moments.
