conclusion: The framework provides a principled ellipsoidal fuzzy-vector representation of mean-covariance information, with covariance encoding interaction, but it is a general mathematical statistics/uncertainty-modeling contribution rather than a quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems result.

title: A Decoupled BDF2-type Integrator For The Spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert System In Ferromagnetic Multilayers
authors: Michele Ald\'e, Dirk Praetorius, Agus L. Soenjaya
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete, linear, decoupled BDF2-type finite element integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (SDLLG) system arising in spintronics. The SDLLG equations couple the magnetization dynamics with a diffusion equation for spin accumulation. The proposed numerical method combines a projection-free BDF2-type tangent-plane discretization of the magnetization dynamics with BDF2 time-stepping for the spin accumulation. By treating the coupling terms explicitly through extrapolation, each time step requires only two independent linear solves that can be performed in parallel. The analysis accommodates the usual exchange field and a general, possibly nonlinear, lower-order effective field. Unconditional weak convergence towards a global weak solution is shown. We also establish bounds on the deviation from the unit-length constraint. Under additional assumptions on the associated energy functional, an energy inequality for the limiting solution is obtained. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper develops and analyzes a fully discrete, linear, decoupled BDF2-type finite element integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert system in ferromagnetic multilayers.
motivation: The SDLLG equations couple magnetization dynamics with spin-accumulation diffusion, and efficient, provably convergent numerical schemes are needed for spintronics simulations.
method: A projection-free BDF2-type tangent-plane discretization for the magnetization is combined with BDF2 time-stepping for spin accumulation, treating coupling terms explicitly via extrapolation so that each step needs only two independent parallel linear solves.
result: Unconditional weak convergence to a global weak solution is proven, along with bounds on the deviation from the unit-length constraint and an energy inequality for the limiting solution under additional energy assumptions; numerical experiments confirm the theory.
conclusion: The scheme offers a practical decoupled solver for SDLLG with rigorous convergence guarantees, though it is a numerical-analysis contribution with no direct quantum-information or thermodynamic content.

title: CrossCheck Ii: A Compiler Plugin For Certified Cost Bounds Of Real-Time C And C++ Code, And Its Evaluation
authors: Luca Dall'olio
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a plugin for the Clang compiler that bounds the cost of C and C++ functions intended for real-time use, and rejects at compile time the functions that allocate, throw, call through pointers, or contain a loop or a recursion for which no bound is found. Loops are bounded by affine ranking potentials synthesized with an SMT solver through Farkas' Lemma, or by logarithmic ones, recursion by depth and size potentials, and callees are analyzed in the calling context in which they are used. For functions in a linear fragment, the plugin emits a cost certificate that a checker, compiled from a Lean~4 definition proved sound in a companion paper, validates with integer arithmetic only; the bound then depends neither on the analyzer nor on the solver. On the 29 kernels of the TACLeBench collection, without annotations, the plugin bounds 142 of 220 loops in the calling contexts of the programs, 131 of them exactly as the benchmarks' flow facts, and 161 of the 165 bounded functions receive a certificate that the checker accepts, 152 of them also validated against an independent description of the source. On the CMSIS-DSP library for Cortex-M (786 functions), with assumed input ranges, it bounds 616 functions. We compare the loop bounds with loop counts observed by running the kernels and with five existing analyzers (LLVM's ScalarEvolution, KoAT2, CoFloCo, Infer and oRange), and the plugin with KoAT2 and CoFloCo on the C programs of the Termination and Complexity Competition: without annotations, 147 of 553 programs receive a certified bound that holds for all inputs, where the two tools bound 288 and 264. Loop bounds, exported annotations and the checker program are also tested on random programs and on mutated certificates.
tldr: The paper presents a Clang compiler plugin that statically bounds the worst-case execution cost of real-time C/C++ functions using affine ranking potentials from an SMT solver and emits machine-checkable cost certificates verified in Lean 4.
motivation: Real-time and safety-critical software needs guaranteed bounds on execution cost, and existing static analyzers give results that depend on the analyzer or solver and are hard to trust; a certified, analyzer-independent bound would improve assurance.
method: Loops are bounded by affine ranking potentials synthesized via Farkas' Lemma in an SMT solver, or by logarithmic potentials, recursion by depth/size potentials, with callees analyzed in calling context; certificates for a linear fragment are checked by a verified Lean 4 checker using only integer arithmetic, and the tool is benchmarked on TACLeBench, CMSIS-DSP, and the Termination and Complexity Competition.
result: On TACLeBench the plugin bounds 142 of 220 loops (131 matching flow facts exactly) and 161 of 165 bounded functions receive accepted certificates; on CMSIS-DSP it bounds 616 of 786 functions, and on the competition suite 147 of 553 programs get certified bounds versus 288 and 264 for KoAT2 and CoFloCo.
conclusion: Certified, solver-independent cost bounds are achievable for a practically relevant fragment of C/C++ and compare favorably in trustworthiness, though coverage is lower than state-of-the-art analyzers.

title: SigK: rPPG-based Key Agreement Scheme For mHealth
authors: Yanping Wang, Lin Li, Leo Yu Zhang, Jianfeng Wang, Chao Chen, Kok-Leong Ong, Jun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As mobile health advances, the use of biomedical sensors for disease monitoring, diagnosis, and treatment is increasing. These sensors often need to be connected through wireless communication technologies to process physiological information from various body parts effectively. Since the data transmitted in these devices usually contain sensitive personal medical information, it is crucial to establish secure communication between devices. In recent studies, the inter-pulse intervals between heartbeats are often used as the key source. They can be extracted from physiological signals such as photoplethysmogram (PPG) or electrocardiogram (ECG), allowing key agreement schemes without pre-key distribution. However, traditional solutions are based on contact measurement devices (e.g., wristbands, chest straps), which limit their applicability in contactless healthcare scenarios. In this paper, we propose a remote PPG-based key agreement scheme to facilitate secure communication between contactless medical devices. We leverage medical devices equipped with cameras to capture remote PPG signals from human faces, and then utilize the signal's power spectral density and peak-peak interval to establish a key agreement with signals synchronously acquired in the Body Area Network (BAN). We have carried out performance evaluations on three publicly available datasets to demonstrate the feasibility of our proposed scheme. In addition, we have also presented a comprehensive proof of the security of our proposed scheme.
tldr: SigK proposes a remote photoplethysmogram (rPPG)-based key agreement scheme for secure communication among contactless mobile-health devices.
motivation: Biomedical sensors in mobile health transmit sensitive data and need secure wireless links without pre-shared keys, but existing PPG/ECG key-agreement methods rely on contact measurements and are unsuitable for contactless healthcare.
method: The scheme captures rPPG signals from facial video using camera-equipped medical devices and derives key material from power spectral density and peak-to-peak intervals, synchronized with signals acquired in a body area network.
result: The authors evaluate the scheme on three public datasets to show feasibility and provide a security proof for the proposed key agreement protocol.
conclusion: Remote PPG can serve as a feasible biometric entropy source for key agreement in contactless mHealth settings, though the work is classical security and not aligned with quantum information research.

title: Joint Trajectory And Power Optimization For Movable-Antenna-Aided Secure Transmission
authors: Jiacheng Liao, Fengchao Zhu, Guojie Hu, Ying Zhang, Tong-Xing Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates joint trajectory and power optimization for movable antenna (MA)-aided secure transmission, where the MA can transmit during its movement. Specifically, the average secrecy rate is maximized subject to movement and power constraints, which couple the MA positions and transmit powers over time, respectively. To tackle this nonconvex problem, we first decouple the transmit powers via Lagrangian duality, where the optimal power for a given trajectory is derived in semi-closed form and shown to depend only on the current MA position. Accordingly, we decouple the MA positions by equivalently reformulating the problem on a discretized linear rail in terms of the farthest grid point and the number of time slots spent at each grid point. Then, from strong duality of the convex relaxation for each farthest point, we construct an asymptotically optimal solution in which the MA dwells at no more than two positions. Finally, a low-complexity dual-based branch-and-bound algorithm is developed to select the farthest grid point and certify the optimality gap. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms the benchmark schemes.
tldr: The paper jointly optimizes the trajectory and transmit power of a movable antenna to maximize the average secrecy rate in a physical-layer secure wireless transmission setting.
motivation: Movable antennas offer an extra spatial degree of freedom, and the authors aim to exploit antenna motion during transmission to improve secrecy against eavesdroppers under movement and power constraints.
method: The nonconvex problem is decoupled via Lagrangian duality for power (semi-closed-form optimal power depending only on current position) and by reformulating the position problem on a discretized linear rail; strong duality of the convex relaxation yields an asymptotically optimal two-position dwell policy, complemented by a low-complexity dual-based branch-and-bound to certify optimality gaps.
result: Simulations show the proposed joint trajectory-and-power design outperforms benchmark schemes in average secrecy rate.
conclusion: Movable-antenna trajectory control combined with power allocation provides a practical means to enhance physical-layer secrecy in wireless systems.

title: Distributed Time-Varying Resource Allocation In Open Networks
authors: Thinh T. Doan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of distributed resource allocation over a team of agents whose active membership changes over time. Each agent's allocation evolves according to its own temporal dynamics, while a shared equality constraint couples all active agents at every instant. For the case of quadratic local objectives, we show that the optimal solution is characterized by a linear system whose coefficient matrix couples a block-tridiagonal temporal structure with a block-diagonal Laplacian capturing the time-varying communication graph. Building on this structure, we develop a distributed forward-backward sweeping algorithm in which each agent resolves its own temporal coupling through a local forward-backward sweep, while the shared resource constraint is resolved through a distributed consensus iteration that is feasible at every iteration. Under a mild diagonal-dominance condition on the temporal coupling, we establish that the optimal allocation at any fixed time converges geometrically to a stationary solution as the horizon grows, and that our distributed algorithm tracks this limit at a matching geometric rate. These results justify a memory-efficient variant of the algorithm in which each agent retains only a bounded window of past history, with the resulting approximation error decaying exponentially in the window size. We validate these theoretical guarantees through numerical simulation, confirming the predicted convergence rates under dynamically changing team membership.
tldr: The paper develops a distributed forward-backward algorithm for time-varying resource allocation in open networks with changing agent membership.
motivation: The work addresses distributed optimization under shared equality constraints when agents join or leave over time and each agent has its own temporal dynamics.
method: For quadratic local objectives, the optimal solution is characterized via a linear system combining block-tridiagonal temporal coupling and a block-diagonal Laplacian, leading to a distributed forward-backward sweep plus consensus iteration.
result: Under diagonal dominance, the fixed-time optimal allocation converges geometrically with the horizon horizon, and the distributed algorithm tracks this limit at a matching rate, enabling a bounded-memory window variant with exponentially decaying error.
conclusion: The proposed method provides convergence and tracking guarantees for distributed resource allocation in dynamic open networks, supported by numerical simulations.

title: An Augmented Generalized Factorization Bound For Generalized Maximum-entropy Sampling
authors: Ananias S. Machado, Marcia Fampa, Jon Lee, Gabriel Ponte
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Li proposed an augmented factorization upper bound for use in branch-and-bound (B&B) algorithms aimed at the maximum entropy sampling problem (MESP). This bound improves on the factorization bound for MESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. GMESP, which selects [MATH] of [MATH] variables so as to maximize the product of the [MATH] greatest eigenvalues of the corresponding principal submatrix of the covariance matrix, is a generalization of MESP (the case [MATH]), and the factorization bound for MESP generalizes to GMESP. We extend the augmentation technique of Li to improve on the generalized factorization bound for GMESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. We derive fundamental properties of the augmented bound, and we develop primal--dual constructions for use within B&B. We give checkable conditions under which the relaxation can be solved in closed form, which always hold when [MATH], at the root and at every subproblem, and a condition under which the closed-form solution is optimal for GMESP. We compare the augmented bound with the spectral bound, establishing an exact comparison for [MATH], an improved worst-case comparison for general [MATH], and sufficient conditions for the dominance of each bound over the other. Computational experiments on benchmark instances show that augmentation can substantially reduce root gaps of the generalized factorization bound, while even reducing its computational time, and that it improves the performance of B&B. Moreover, a hybrid strategy that uses the trace upper bound to prune nodes and the closed-form certificate to avoid solving the relaxation can significantly accelerate B&B when [MATH] is small.
tldr: The paper develops an augmented generalized factorization upper bound for branch-and-bound algorithms solving the generalized maximum-entropy sampling problem (GMESP).
motivation: MESP and its generalization GMESP are hard combinatorial optimization problems where tight, cheaply computable upper bounds are essential for practical branch-and-bound performance; existing factorization bounds can be improved when the covariance matrix is positive definite.
method: The authors extend Li's augmentation technique from the factorization bound for MESP to the generalized factorization bound for GMESP, derive structural properties of the augmented bound, build primal-dual constructions for use inside branch-and-bound, and give closed-form solvability conditions.
result: They establish closed-form solution conditions (always holding for small m at the root and all subproblems), prove optimality conditions, compare the bound exactly with the spectral bound for m=2 and give improved worst-case and dominance conditions for general m, and show on benchmarks substantially reduced root gaps and faster branch-and-bound.
conclusion: Augmentation yields tighter and often cheaper bounds than the generalized factorization bound, and a hybrid trace-bound pruning plus closed-form certificate strategy markedly accelerates branch-and-bound for small m.

title: Generating Health Variables For A Synthetic Population Of Santa Catarina, Brazil, Via Ensemble Learning And A Calibrated Linear Program
authors: Vitoria Caroline Blau Maria Eduarda Pinheiro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Sa\'ude (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.
tldr: The paper generates health-related variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, using ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program.
motivation: Agent-based epidemiological models require synthetic populations with health attributes, but in Brazil such data are only available from sample surveys like the PNS.
method: Class probabilities are estimated with an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes via a linear program that reproduces survey-estimated class proportions.
result: The authors show that under a mild condition satisfied by their ensemble, the penalty term is unnecessary and proportions are reproduced exactly; cross-validation on PNS data yields the best results.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively adds health variables to a georeferenced synthetic population and outperforms alternatives in cross-validation.

title: Normal And Unitary Operators On Smooth Banach Spaces Via The Duality Mapping
authors: Deepesh K. P Mohammed Shameem
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article extends the classical notions of normal and unitary operators from Hilbert spaces to smooth Banach spaces through the duality mapping. The class of normal operators introduced in this setting contains, as a special case, the self-adjoint operators on smooth Banach spaces defined via the duality mapping. We establish several characterisations of these operators and investigate their fundamental properties. In particular, we examine various spectral properties of normal operators on smooth Banach spaces. These results demonstrate that many fundamental aspects of the classical theory of normal and unitary operators on Hilbert spaces persist in the smooth Banach space setting.
tldr: The paper generalizes normal and unitary operators from Hilbert spaces to smooth Banach spaces using the duality mapping, establishing characterizations and spectral properties.
motivation: Classical notions of normal and unitary operators are tied to Hilbert space inner products; the authors aim to extend them to the broader setting of smooth Banach spaces where an inner product is unavailable.
method: The duality mapping is used to define analogues of self-adjoint, normal, and unitary operators on smooth Banach spaces, followed by derivation of characterizations and spectral-theoretic results.
result: Several characterizations of these generalized normal and unitary operators are established, and their spectral properties are shown to parallel many features of the Hilbert-space theory.
conclusion: Many fundamental aspects of the classical theory of normal and unitary operators persist in smooth Banach spaces, suggesting the duality-mapping approach is a viable generalization.

title: Linearization For Unbounded Perturbations Of Sublinear Growth
authors: Jiangqiong Yu Xiao Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound. We obtain representations of the displacement in terms of stable and unstable orbit series that converge uniformly on any bounded set and give the inverse conjugacy by using the Banach fixed points theorem in a weighted function space.
tldr: We prove global topological linearization theorems for dynamical systems with unbounded perturbations whose growth is sublinear, including growth bounds and uniqueness of the conjugacy.
motivation: Classical Hartman-Grobman-type linearization results typically assume bounded or sufficiently controlled perturbations; the authors extend this to unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth under a spectral gap condition.
method: We assume a spectral gap and a small Lipschitz constant, represent the displacement of the conjugacy via stable and unstable orbit series, and construct the inverse by applying the Banach fixed point theorem in a weighted function space.
result: The conjugacy and its inverse deviate from the identity by no more than the growth bound of the perturbation; the series converge uniformly on bounded sets, and the conjugacy is unique within this class of maps.
conclusion: Sublinear unbounded perturbations admit unique topological linearization with matching growth bounds, extending the classical theory beyond the bounded-perturbation regime.

title: Symmetry-reduced High-index Saddle Dynamics For Saddle Point Search Under Continuous Symmetries
authors: Yuanshen Lin, Jianyuan Yin, Lei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For energy invariant under continuous symmetries, critical points may form critical manifolds, leading to degeneracy of the Hessian. In such cases, the ascent directions in high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) may include symmetry directions, making it difficult to locate saddle points of a prescribed Morse index. To address this issue, we propose symmetry-reduced HiSD (SR-HiSD) by formulating the quotient HiSD on the quotient manifold and horizontally lifting the dynamics to the ambient Hilbert space. Under suitable regularity and Morse--Bott assumptions, we establish local exponential stability of the quotient HiSD equilibria associated with the prescribed index and instability of equilibria associated with critical points of different indices. We further prove local convergence of the SR-HiSD position trajectory to a single point on the target critical orbit. Numerical algorithms with direction updates restricted to the horizontal space are developed. Numerical experiments on Morse clusters, the Onsager model, and the Landau--Brazovskii model demonstrate reliable searches for saddle points of the prescribed index and the construction of solution landscapes, together with improved computational efficiency in large-scale problems.
tldr: The authors propose a symmetry-reduced high-index saddle dynamics (SR-HiSD) method that formulates the dynamics on a quotient manifold to find saddle points of a prescribed Morse index in systems with continuous symmetries.
motivation: For energies invariant under continuous symmetries, critical points form critical manifolds and the Hessian becomes degenerate, so ascent directions in high-index saddle dynamics can align with symmetry directions and prevent locating saddle points of the desired index.
method: They formulate a quotient HiSD on the quotient manifold and horizontally lift the dynamics to the ambient Hilbert space, restricting direction updates to the horizontal space, and analyze local exponential stability and convergence under Morse-Bott-type assumptions.
result: They prove local exponential stability of quotient equilibria with the prescribed index and instability of those with different indices, and prove convergence of the position trajectory to a single point on the target critical orbit; numerical tests on Morse clusters, the Onsager model, and the Landau-Brazovskii model confirm reliable searches and improved efficiency.
conclusion: SR-HiSD provides a robust and efficient framework for computing index-constrained saddle points and solution landscapes in symmetric energy models.

title: Subnormality Of $B$-operators Of Class $\mathscr{S}$
authors: Sameer Chavan, Zenon Jan Jab{\l}o\'nski, Il Bong Jung, Jan Stochel
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize subnormality of [MATH]-operators [MATH] on [MATH], where [MATH] is an isometry, [MATH], [MATH] is subnormal, and [MATH]. We determine when [MATH] admits compactly supported signed elementary measures and express them explicitly in terms of the elementary measures of [MATH]. Requiring the signed elementary measures of [MATH] to be positive yields a complete measure-theoretic characterization of the subnormality of [MATH]. If [MATH] is injective, [MATH] is subnormal if and only if it is a contraction. In the general case, the subnormality of [MATH] is equivalent to the contractivity of its restriction to [MATH]. We also obtain equivalent criteria involving the Taylor spectra of [MATH], its minimal normal and minimal quasinormal extensions, and the corresponding pairs of moduli. These results extend the characterization previously known for a quasinormal lower-right entry.
tldr: A pure operator-theory paper characterizing subnormality of B-operators of class S via signed elementary measures and Taylor spectra.
motivation: Subnormality criteria for operator tuples built from isometries and subnormal entries are of interest in multivariable spectral theory, extending known results for quasinormal lower-right entries.
method: The authors construct compactly supported signed elementary measures for the operator and relate them explicitly to the elementary measures of the subnormal entry, plus analyze Taylor spectra and minimal normal/quasinormal extensions.
result: Subnormality is fully characterized by positivity of the signed elementary measures; for injective cases it reduces to contractivity, and in general to contractivity of a restriction.
conclusion: The work yields measure-theoretic and spectral criteria for subnormality of class-S B-operators, generalizing earlier quasinormal-entry results.

title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity In A Proof Kernel And In Lean/Mathlib
authors: Nikolaos Nikolaou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge. We also need to know whether a "new proof" is indeed new, whether a thousand generated proofs contain one idea or many, and where each sits relative to human mathematics. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. Following Hilbert's 24th problem and the identity-of-proofs problem, we ask how far apart two proofs of one theorem are, and what shape the proof space they inhabit has. We define 19 dissimilarity measures in 6 families (syntactic, structural, dependency & resource, semantic, information-theoretic, higher-categorical) and 10 desirable properties, which we argue are the conditions for safely optimising a measure. In a Curry-Howard kernel, 5 machine-checked proofs that the primes are infinite show that raw syntax cannot tell a rewrite from a new argument, that dependency-based and structural measures reproduce the intuitive ordering (Euclid rewritten < Goldbach < Furstenberg), and that semantic measures invert it: Furstenberg's topological proof produces exactly Euclid's witness. A replication in Lean 4/Mathlib (3 theorems, 19 proofs, 18 measures) confirms that dependency-closure measures track intuition best, and shows that equality of normal forms never holds between differently written versions of the same argument, that proofs by citation look unlike the arguments they cite, and that proof irrelevance cannot distinguish any two proofs. We argue for reporting dissimilarity as a multi-level profile, extend the measures to proofs of different theorems, and discuss uses, from detecting duplicated AI proofs and orchestrating prover agents to interpreting AI proofs via their nearest human-understandable counterparts. Code, Lean sources and data are released.
tldr: The paper defines 19 dissimilarity measures across six families (syntactic, structural, dependency, semantic, information-theoretic, higher-categorical) to quantify how far apart two proofs of the same theorem are, validated in a Curry-Howard proof kernel and in Lean 4/Mathlib.
motivation: Machine-generated mathematics produces proofs faster than humans can assess them, so we need principled notions of proof identity and distance to detect duplication, cluster ideas, and relate AI proofs to human ones — a modern take on Hilbert's 24th problem.
method: The authors formalize ten desirable properties for a proof metric, implement 19 measures in a Curry-Howard kernel on five machine-checked proofs of the infinitude of primes, and replicate the analysis in Lean 4/Mathlib with 18 measures over 19 proofs of three theorems.
result: Dependency-closure and structural measures best track intuitive ordering (Euclid rewritten < Goldbach < Furstenberg), semantic measures invert it since Furstenberg's proof yields Euclid's witness, and equality of normal forms or proof irrelevance never distinguishes differently written versions of the same argument.
conclusion: Proof dissimilarity should be reported as a multi-level profile rather than a single scalar, with applications to detecting duplicated AI proofs, orchestrating prover agents, and interpreting machine proofs via nearest human counterparts.

title: Bit-Flip Attacks On Quantized Neural Networks Without Knowledge Of Model Parameters
authors: Mahmoud Abumandour, Srinija Ramichetty, Guru Venkataramani, Alaa R. Alameldeen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.32128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that quantization asymmetry concentrates bit-flip vulnerability in small tensors retained at high precision. CoarseHammer targets these tensors and accepts flips at any bit, without parameter values, gradients, or data. It remains effective under continued fine-tuning. Under ideal placement, CoarseHammer reaches chance accuracy in at least 81.5% of runs on each of ten evaluated models, including four large language models, with median successful runs requiring at most 24 flips. On simulated DRAM with 0.01 flippable bits per million, it outperforms three prior attacks on every evaluated convolutional network, succeeding in up to 83.6% of runs while they never succeed. On a real system, CoarseHammer steers heap-allocated tensors onto vulnerable frames despite address space layout randomization, without accessing the model file. With 16 templated frames, median accuracy reaches chance for all four language models and approximately chance for four convolutional networks.
tldr: CoarseHammer is a parameter-agnostic bit-flip attack that exploits quantization asymmetry to concentrate vulnerability in small high-precision tensors of quantized neural networks, degrading them to chance accuracy with few flips.
motivation: Quantized neural networks are deployed widely, and their memory-level fault susceptibility is poorly understood; prior bit-flip attacks require knowledge of model parameters, gradients, or data, limiting realism.
method: The authors identify that quantization asymmetries leave a few small tensors in high precision, then design a blind attack that flips bits at arbitrary positions in those tensors, validated with ideal placement simulations, simulated DRAM fault models, and a real-system heap-grooming demonstration that defeats ASLR without reading the model file.
result: Under ideal placement the attack reaches chance accuracy in at least 81.5% of runs across ten models (including four LLMs) with a median of at most 24 flips; on simulated DRAM it outperforms three prior attacks on every CNN tested, and on a real system 16 templated frames suffice to bring all four LLMs to chance accuracy.
conclusion: Quantization-aware allocation creates a concentrated, easily exploitable fault-injection surface, arguing for hardened tensor placement and fault-tolerant deployment of quantized models.

title: Condensates And Edge Effects In The Generalised Takayasu Model
authors: Angad Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, in the 1D Takayasu Mass Model (MM) of diffusion-aggregation with input, large condensates and a novel power law were observed in simulations, and later characterised exactly. We extend these studies to the Takayasu model with generalised input, and provide a relation to translate the distribution function of the MM to any model with a space and time independent injection process. In the 1D Charge Model (CM) of a system of size [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] charge monomers are injected with equal probability at each site in each time step, there is a power law distribution of cluster charge [MATH]. This distribution cuts off at [MATH] in the steady state for long times [MATH] and a large charge condensate forms with a net charge between [MATH] and [MATH]. A distance dependent distribution function is observed around the charge condensate and near open boundaries, both of which act like an edge in the system, analogous to the observations in the MM. The charge distribution measured at a distance [MATH] from the edge transitions from the previously known CM bulk power law [MATH] for small clusters ([MATH]), to a novel power law [MATH] for larger clusters ([MATH]). In the 1D Pair Injection Model (PIM), where [MATH] and [MATH] charge monomers are injected simultaneously at adjacent sites, the power law distribution [MATH] cuts off at [MATH] in the steady state for long times, and no large growing condensate is formed. We still observe a distance dependent distribution measured from the largest clusters, or an open boundary, with a bulk power law [MATH] for small clusters ([MATH]), and an edge power law [MATH] for larger clusters ([MATH]).
tldr: This paper extends the classical 1D Takayasu diffusion-aggregation model with generalized input, deriving condensate formation and edge-dependent cluster-charge distributions.
motivation: The study is motivated by recently observed large condensates and novel power laws in the 1D Takayasu Mass Model, aiming to characterize them for generalized injection processes.
method: The author analyzes classical stochastic aggregation models—the Charge Model and Pair Injection Model—using exact relations and simulation-inspired distribution functions for steady-state cluster charges.
result: The Charge Model exhibits a large condensate and a bulk-to-edge transition from a known power law to a novel power law, while the Pair Injection Model shows no growing condensate but still displays edge-dependent distributions.
conclusion: Generalized input processes produce condensates and boundary effects analogous to those in the Takayasu Mass Model, with distinct power-law behavior near edges and condensates.

title: Theory Of Modulation Instability For Coupled Microresonators
authors: Andrey Gelash Alena Kolesnikova
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thanks to hybridization phenomena, coupled microresonator systems enable modulation instability (MI) of the continuous wave background field across all possible dispersion combinations: anomalous-anomalous, normal-normal, and anomalous-normal microrings. Here, using the Lugiato-Lefever model in the supermode basis for two coupled microresonators with arbitrary second-order dispersion coefficients, arbitrary losses, and coupling strength, we derive a general eigenvalue problem for the [MATH] matrix. We consider the regime of resonance splitting, in which the pump couples only to one of the two supermodes, allowing us to obtain analytical expressions for the stationary continuous-wave field distributed over the coupled system. When the microresonators have similar geometry, the antidiagonal elements of the eigenvalue-problem matrix nearly vanish, and we obtain a fully analytical solution for the MI gain rate for the entire range of coupled microresonator devices. Finally, we investigate cases in which the analytical treatment must be supplemented with more accurate numerical solutions of the MI eigenvalue problem, though even then the analytical theory captures the main features of the four-wave mixing process and the gain-rate behavior.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical theory of modulation instability in coupled microresonators using the Lugiato-Lefever model in a supermode basis.
motivation: Coupled microresonator systems can exhibit modulation instability across all dispersion combinations due to hybridization, but a general analytical treatment for arbitrary losses, coupling, and dispersion is needed.
method: The authors formulate a general eigenvalue problem for the modulation instability matrix in the supermode basis and derive analytical expressions for the continuous-wave field and gain rate in the resonance-splitting regime.
result: They obtain a fully analytical solution for the modulation instability gain rate when the microresonators have similar geometry, and identify regimes where numerical solutions are required but the analytical theory still captures the main four-wave mixing features.
conclusion: The theory provides a general framework for understanding modulation instability in coupled microresonators and can guide the design of such devices across different dispersion regimes.

title: On The Computation Of Green's Function In Layered Elastic Media
authors: Heng Yuan, Wenzhong Zhang, Bo Wang, Wei Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.
tldr: The paper presents a recursive scheme for computing time-harmonic elastodynamic Green's functions in three-dimensional layered elastic media.
motivation: Efficient and stable computation of Green's functions in layered elastic media is needed as a foundation for analyzing and numerically simulating elastic wave scattering.
method: Using a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain combined with classical interface reaction-transmission theory, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH and P-SV components described by five scalar functions solved recursively at linear cost in the number of layers.
result: The recursion yields a stable numerical method suitable for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, independent of where source and target points lie in the layer stack.
conclusion: The scheme provides a scalable computational foundation for elastic wave scattering analysis and simulation in layered media.

title: One Release For All: Private Simple Linear Regression Via Improved Simplex Mapping
authors: Anshoo Tandon Sasmita Harini S
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a single-release extension of DP-RSS for private simple linear regression when both input and output are bounded in [MATH]. Rather than privately releasing several related sufficient-statistic estimates, we encode the required information in one unit-sensitivity vector and apply the Laplace mechanism once at the full privacy budget. The required least-squares sufficient statistics are then recovered by deterministic post-processing and used directly in an ordinary least-squares solve. We obtain variance reductions of [MATH]--[MATH] relative to DP-RSS for several statistics. Experiments show that the benefit is most pronounced in the high-privacy regime, while the methods converge as privacy noise becomes negligible.
tldr: The paper proposes a single-release differentially private method for simple linear regression using an improved simplex mapping and one Laplace mechanism application.
motivation: Private simple linear regression typically requires releasing several sufficient-statistic estimates, which can increase noise; the authors aim to encode the needed statistics into one unit-sensitivity vector to reduce variance.
method: They extend DP-RSS by privately releasing a single unit-sensitivity vector under the full privacy budget using the Laplace mechanism, then recover least-squares sufficient statistics via deterministic post-processing for an ordinary least-squares solve.
result: The method achieves variance reductions relative to DP-RSS for several statistics, with the largest benefit in the high-privacy regime, while both approaches converge when privacy noise is negligible.
conclusion: A one-release simplex-mapping approach improves private simple linear regression accuracy, especially under strong privacy constraints, but the work is in classical differential privacy and statistics rather than quantum information.

title: Analysis And Optimal Approximation Of Operator-Valued Riccati Equations With Unbounded Control Operators
authors: James Cheung
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present new results on the well-posedness and approximation of the operator-valued Riccati equations that arise in the context of control systems with unbounded control operators, e.g. interior point and boundary control systems. We first prove that the Bochner integral form of the operator-valued Riccati equation is well-posed even if the control operator is unbounded. We then leverage the favorable structure of the Bochner integral form to prove that the error of approximate solutions are bounded by the approximation error of the process [MATH]-semigroup. This general result then leads to the correct prediction of optimal error estimates for the finite element approximation of the Riccati equation. The analysis is carried out on both the time-dependent and stationary Riccati equations and our numerical convergence study on the weakly damped wave process and the thermal process with delta function actuation operators corroborate the results of our analysis.
tldr: The paper establishes well-posedness and optimal finite-element approximation error estimates for operator-valued Riccati equations arising in control systems with unbounded control operators.
motivation: Riccati equations with unbounded control operators (interior point and boundary control) are common in control of distributed-parameter systems, but well-posedness and error analysis were not fully established for the Bochner integral formulation.
method: The authors prove well-posedness of the Bochner integral form of the Riccati equation for unbounded control operators and bound approximation errors by the approximation error of the process semigroup, then apply this to finite element discretizations of time-dependent and stationary Riccati equations.
result: The general semigroup-based error bound yields optimal finite element error estimates, corroborated by numerical convergence studies on a weakly damped wave process and a thermal process with delta-function actuation.
conclusion: The Bochner integral formulation provides a clean framework for well-posedness and optimal approximation of operator Riccati equations with unbounded control, with numerical evidence supporting the theory.

title: The Work Of Mathematical Production In The Age Of Ai
authors: Thomas Koberda Asaf Hadari
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of powerful artificial intelligence has unsettled the relationship between mathematical production and the human intellectual activity that mathematical artifacts have traditionally documented. We argue that mathematical practice cannot be adequately understood through the production of mathematical knowledge alone, and distinguish four interrelated dimensions of inquiry: knowledge, understanding, making sense, and figuring out. Building on Kitcher, Dewey, and subsequent philosophy of mathematical practice, we develop an expanded framework incorporating the cognitive and computational capacities of mathematical communities, their conceptual organizations, provisional investigative models, and the role of unsuccessful inquiry. We propose reconceptualizing artificial intelligence as a manifestation of physically organized computation whose mathematical behavior itself can become an object of experimental investigation. This perspective motivates a program of , by which we mean the construction and comparison of artificial intellectual communities developing mathematical practices under different cognitive, conceptual, and normative conditions. Our aim is not simply to automate mathematical research or increase the production of theorems, but to investigate the robustness and contingency of mathematical concepts, the possibilities of alternative mathematical practices, and what such investigations might reveal about human mathematical cognition. Finally, we consider the future of human intellectual agency in a world where mathematical production need no longer depend upon humans. We argue for intergenerational epistemic stewardship as a justification for sustaining human mathematical traditions and opportunities for intellectual participation, independently of humanity's continued indispensability to mathematical progress.
tldr: The paper argues for an expanded philosophical framework of mathematical practice and proposes studying AI as physically organized computation through artificial intellectual communities.
motivation: AI's growing role in mathematical production unsettles traditional accounts of mathematics as documenting human intellectual activity, motivating a richer account of mathematical practice beyond mere theorem production.
method: The authors build on Kitcher, Dewey, and philosophy of mathematical practice to distinguish knowledge, understanding, making sense, and figuring out, and propose experimental comparison of artificial intellectual communities.
result: They develop a conceptual framework for investigating the robustness and contingency of mathematical concepts and alternative mathematical practices, and argue for intergenerational epistemic stewardship.
conclusion: The paper is a philosophy-of-mathematics and AI-ethics contribution, not a technical result in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Service Location Flexibility In Dynamic Vehicle Routing
authors: G\'erard P. Cachon, Bora Cetin, Sophie H. Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parcel lockers and delivery robots let a vehicle serve customers at nearby locations. We study this service location flexibility in the dynamic traveling repairman problem, where a single vehicle may serve each demand anywhere within a radius [MATH] of its location. Arrivals form a Poisson process, demand locations are independent and uniform in the unit square, and on-site service times are i.i.d. with uniformly bounded second moments, where the radius [MATH] may vary across systems as the on-site load [MATH] tends to one. In this heavy-traffic regime, the optimal mean system time is of order [MATH], compared with [MATH] without service location flexibility [BvR91, PFB11]. Thus, flexibility reduces the order of optimal mean system time when [MATH] stays fixed or shrinks more slowly than [MATH]. Moreover, when [MATH] is on the order of [MATH] or larger, the vehicle can attain the optimal order by repeating a fixed covering route that passes within [MATH] of every location. For example, the vehicle can follow a fixed grid route through parcel lockers, with customers in each square cell sharing the locker at its center.
tldr: This paper studies service location flexibility in dynamic vehicle routing, where a single vehicle can serve demands at nearby locations such as parcel lockers or delivery robots.
motivation: The authors are motivated by new delivery modes that allow customers to be served at flexible nearby locations rather than their exact addresses, and they aim to understand the resulting impact on system performance in heavy traffic.
method: The paper analyzes the dynamic traveling repairman problem with Poisson arrivals, uniformly distributed demand, and service radius flexibility, deriving asymptotic optimal mean system time in a heavy-traffic regime.
result: Service location flexibility reduces the order of optimal mean system time compared with the rigid-location case, and when the service radius is sufficiently large, a fixed covering route can achieve the optimal order.
conclusion: Flexible service locations can fundamentally improve dynamic vehicle routing performance, with fixed covering routes such as parcel-locker grids providing order-optimal strategies in certain regimes.

title: Two-Sided Weighted-History Transfer For Abstract Systems With Infinite Memory
authors: Gossrin Jean-Marc Bomisso
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a two-sided transfer principle for second-order systems with Hilbert-valued infinite memory. The squared norm of the coupled semigroup, from a centered weighted-history space into the energy space, is bounded above and below by constant multiples of [MATH]. Here [MATH] is the squared norm of the right-translation semigroup between the corresponding weighted and unweighted memory spaces. The coupled system satisfies an energy identity, a mechanical multiplier estimate and a bounded observation. The memory density has decay of order at most polynomial, and the weight is admissible. Under these hypotheses the energy is bounded by the initial norm times [MATH], where [MATH] is the tail of the kernel. The two-sided equivalence holds when [MATH] is integrable and the kernel has a finite first moment and satisfies a tail bound, or when [MATH]. For the density [MATH], with [MATH] and [MATH], and the weight [MATH], with [MATH], the rate is [MATH]. For kernels and weights with logarithmic factors, under explicit conditions on the exponents, the logarithm of the weight enters the rate below the saturation threshold, and the logarithm of the kernel enters above it. A theorem with a prescribed decay of the inherited history gives exact exponents for algebraically growing histories. The hypotheses are verified for gradient-memory waves without instantaneous damping, endpoint-damped strings, damped plates and oscillators.
tldr: The paper proves a two-sided weighted-history transfer principle for abstract second-order systems with Hilbert-valued infinite memory and derives energy decay rates.
motivation: The work aims to characterize energy decay for systems with infinite memory by relating coupled semigroup norms to weighted and unweighted memory-space translation semigroups.
method: It establishes upper and lower bounds via semigroup theory, energy identities, multiplier estimates, and admissible weights under kernel tail and moment assumptions.
result: Two-sided equivalence holds under integrability or first-moment/tail conditions, with explicit rates for algebraic kernels and logarithmic corrections below or above a saturation threshold.
conclusion: The framework provides exact decay exponents for several PDE examples, including gradient-memory waves, damped strings, plates, and oscillators, but it is purely mathematical and not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sharp History-Length Dependence Of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates For A Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
authors: Gossrin Jean-Marc Bomisso
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length [MATH] grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--[MATH] generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of [MATH]. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed [MATH]. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to [MATH]. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale [MATH], uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on [MATH]. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order [MATH] for the truncated generator and of order [MATH] after discretization, improved to [MATH] at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.
tldr: The paper proves mesh-uniform, sharp bounds on the loss of exponential stability for a boundary-memory Euler–Bernoulli beam as the retained history length grows.
motivation: Boundary-memory (viscoelastic) damping models require truncating the history for computation, so one must understand how exponential stability degrades with the retained history length and whether this behaviour is robust under discretization.
method: Analysis of continuous and conforming Hermite finite-element generators for the augmented (state + history) system, deriving upper and lower resolvent-norm bounds at zero frequency that are uniform in the beam mesh and history mesh, plus strong-convergence and residual-order estimates, verified numerically.
result: Zero-frequency resolvent norms scale as constant multiples of the history length M, semigroup norms exhibit a plateau of duration proportional to M, and matching exponential estimates hold with optimal time scale uniformly in the meshes; remote-history packets yield residuals of order 1/M (improved at zero frequency).
conclusion: The loss of exponential stability from history truncation is sharply quantified and is independent of spatial discretization, yielding convergent finite-history approximations to the full-history semigroup.

title: Sharp Hellinger Risk Of The Multivariate Gaussian Npmle
authors: Zheng Li Xingzhou Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For multivariate Gaussian location mixtures whose mixing distributions have coordinatewise sub-Gaussian tails, we prove that the unconstrained nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator attains the minimax rate [MATH] under squared Hellinger loss. This holds for every fixed dimension [MATH] and every fixed tail parameter [MATH]. The upper bound applies to every measurable choice of a global likelihood maximizer and improves the earlier bound of order [MATH] by a factor of [MATH]. A key step is a sharp bracketing bound for multivariate polynomials. For the [MATH] unit ball of real polynomials in [MATH] variables with total degree at most [MATH], the log bracketing number at width [MATH] is at most [MATH] for [MATH]. The constant [MATH] depends only on [MATH]. The bound holds for every positive Borel measure [MATH] under which each nonzero polynomial in the space has a finite, positive [MATH] norm. We prove the bound using volume estimates for a complex Veronese cone and Gaussian small-ball probabilities, then apply it to bound the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of Gaussian mixture densities. We obtain the matching minimax lower bound by adapting the Hermite perturbation construction of Kim and Guntuboyina.
tldr: The paper establishes sharp minimax Hellinger-risk guarantees for the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator of multivariate Gaussian location mixtures under coordinatewise sub-Gaussian tails.
motivation: The work seeks to sharpen existing risk bounds for Gaussian mixture density estimation and close the gap between upper and lower minimax rates under squared Hellinger loss.
method: It proves a sharp bracketing-number bound for multivariate polynomials using volume estimates for a complex Veronese cone and Gaussian small-ball probabilities, then applies this to bound local Hellinger bracketing entropy for Gaussian mixtures; the lower bound adapts a Hermite perturbation construction.
result: The unconstrained NPMLE attains the minimax rate for every fixed dimension and tail parameter, improving the earlier upper bound by a logarithmic factor, with a matching minimax lower bound.
conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous nonparametric statistics result on optimal Hellinger risk for Gaussian mixture estimation, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz Under Pointwise Commutation
authors: Feng Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic convergence of the corresponding sparse moment--SOS hierarchy for polynomial matrix optimization. We also derive a criterion for finite convergence of moment relaxation and extraction of a global minimizer based on local flatness and consistency of the local representing matrix measures on overlapping variable blocks. Finally, we provide a sufficient construction of commuting decompositions through linear equations, using a reference polynomial matrix with a simple spectrum at some point.
tldr: The paper proves a matrix Positivstellensatz for sparse polynomial matrix optimization under correlative sparsity, running intersection, local Archimedean conditions, and an added pointwise commutation requirement, yielding convergent sparse moment-SOS hierarchies.
motivation: The scalar correlative-sparsity Positivstellensatz enables compact moment-SOS relaxations, but its matrix analogue fails even with standard sparsity and Archimedean assumptions, blocking efficient semidefinite relaxations for polynomial matrix optimization.
method: Assuming a pointwise commutation condition, the authors build central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, avoiding any need for a global measure extension.
result: Positive definiteness on the feasible set is shown to imply membership in the sum of local matrix quadratic modules, giving asymptotic convergence of the sparse moment-SOS hierarchy plus a finite-convergence criterion and global minimizer extraction via local flatness; a linear-equation construction of commuting decompositions is also given.
conclusion: The work extends Positivstellensatz-type certificates to the matrix-valued sparse setting under a commutation restriction, providing a practical route to scalable semidefinite relaxations for polynomial matrix programs.

title: A Sequential Quadratic Programming Perspective On Optimal Control
authors: Suman Chakravorty Abhijeet
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR), Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), and Newton's method for optimal control problems. Using a unified Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework, we introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based algorithm that solves for the exact Newton step the optimal control problem. Within this framework, we establish that iLQR is a principled modified SQP method rather than merely an approximation of DDP. We show that iLQR generates a descent direction, whereas the inclusion of dynamics Hessians in DDP and Newton-LQR may lead to indefinite quadratic subproblems and necessitate regularization. We further distinguish DDP and the proposed Newton-LQR algorithm through their treatment of costate information and second-order dynamics terms. Numerical experiments across six benchmark problems demonstrate that iLQR often exhibits superior convergence during the initial optimization phase, while Newton-LQR and DDP can exploit second-order information to accelerate convergence near a solution.
tldr: The paper analyzes iLQR, DDP, and a new Newton-LQR algorithm for optimal control through a unified sequential quadratic programming framework.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the theoretical relationships among iterative LQR, differential dynamic programming, and Newton's method for optimal control problems.
method: They formulate these algorithms within an SQP framework and introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based method that computes exact Newton steps, then compare costate treatment and second-order dynamics terms.
result: Numerical experiments on six benchmark problems show that iLQR often converges faster initially, while Newton-LQR and DDP can exploit second-order information to accelerate convergence near a solution.
conclusion: The work positions iLQR as a principled modified SQP method and distinguishes DDP and Newton-LQR by their handling of second-order dynamics and costate information.

title: Gradient-free Mcmc Exploiting Low-dimensional Gaussian And nonGaussian Posterior Structure
authors: Hongqiao Wang, Jiahua Jiang, Jing Liu, Jinglai Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for Bayesian inverse problems is expensive: the unknown is high-dimensional, every likelihood evaluation requires a forward solve, and gradients are often unavailable. The posterior typically differs from the prior in a few directions and is often approximately Gaussian in most of them but strongly non-Gaussian in a few. We propose the NQU sampler, a gradient-free MCMC method that splits the parameter space into non-Gaussian (N), approximately quadratic (Q) and uninformative (U) directions. The split is learned once, before sampling, from likelihood values, and each block is updated by a kernel suited to it; a collapsed update handles a global prior scale. Because the learned structure only shapes the proposals, every update leaves the exact posterior invariant, at the cost of one likelihood evaluation. We give a condition under which the blocks can be learned and show that, for likelihoods with exactly the learned structure, the spectral gap of the sampler does not depend on the dimension, whereas updating the scale given all coordinates can have a gap of order [MATH]. On the posterior axes, the NQU sampler, learning included, needed the fewest evaluations in four of five synthetic examples with [MATH], among nine baselines including gradient-based ones; in those with non-Gaussian directions, gradient-free baselines needed at least ten times as many. On a methane ignition problem with 219 uncertain rate constants, it gave consistent estimates, whereas full-space robust adaptive Metropolis needed about 300 times as many evaluations and an ensemble sampler degenerated.
tldr: The paper proposes NQU, a gradient-free MCMC sampler that learns a split of the parameter space into non-Gaussian, approximately quadratic, and uninformative directions to accelerate Bayesian inverse problems.
motivation: MCMC for high-dimensional Bayesian inverse problems is expensive because each likelihood evaluation requires a forward solve and gradients are often unavailable. Posterior structure is often low-dimensional, with only a few non-Gaussian directions.
method: The authors learn a block decomposition of the parameter space from likelihood evaluations before sampling, then use tailored kernels for each block plus a collapsed update for a global prior scale, keeping the exact posterior invariant.
result: The sampler achieves dimension-independent spectral gap under an exact-structure condition, and empirically needed the fewest likelihood evaluations in four of five synthetic examples, with large gains on a 219-parameter methane ignition problem.
conclusion: Exploiting learned low-dimensional posterior structure can substantially reduce the cost of gradient-free MCMC in Bayesian inverse problems.

title: Viscosity Solutions Of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations With Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
authors: Qi Zhang Zihao Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a L\'evy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.
tags: backward stochastic differential equations with jumps
tldr: The paper studies viscosity solutions for parabolic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman integro-differential equations arising in stochastic recursive control with jumps and non-Lipschitz running costs.
motivation: The authors aim to handle recursive stochastic control problems with Levy-type operators and nonlocal running costs under weaker regularity assumptions than Lipschitz continuity.
method: They establish well-posedness, comparison, and stability for backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, derive a dynamic programming principle, and use approximation and viscosity-solution stability arguments.
result: The value function is shown to be a viscosity solution of the corresponding HJB integro-differential equation, and a comparison principle yields uniqueness within a prescribed growth class under a uniform jump-amplitude bound.
conclusion: The work extends viscosity-solution theory for HJB integro-differential equations to non-Lipschitz settings relevant to jump-diffusion recursive control, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
keywords: backward stochastic differential equations with jumps

title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators On Locally Finite Trees
authors: Fayou Zhao Chenghao Xiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, [MATH] and [MATH], on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp [MATH] boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator [MATH] and the triangular maximal operator [MATH] on a prototypical tree, proving that the former's region strictly contains the latter's for all [MATH].
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators on locally finite trees, establishing boundedness and comparison results.
motivation: Ball-type maximal operators on trees are natural analogues of classical maximal functions, but their fractional triangular variants and their precise relation to classical fractional maximal operators have not been systematically characterized.
method: The authors develop a geometric tool based on families of overlapping triangles whose total measure is comparable to a ball, then use it to prove pointwise comparisons and sharp L^p boundedness with explicit exponent ranges, validating optimality via counterexamples.
result: They obtain complete pointwise comparisons among triangular and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees, sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees, sharp L^p bounds, and show that the unboundedness region of the ball-type operator strictly contains that of the triangular operator on a prototypical tree.
conclusion: The work provides a thorough geometric and harmonic-analytic classification of triangular fractional maximal operators on trees, highlighting how tree geometry affects boundedness behavior.

title: Gradient Descent Achieves $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ Convergence
authors: Xiaotian Jiang Chang He
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent on a lower-bounded nonconvex function with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and Hessian. Classical analysis shows that a fixed stepsize guarantees a decrease of order [MATH] per update. In contrast, our rule uses a sequence of [MATH] updates with a total stepsize of order [MATH]. We establish a weighted descent inequality for every prefix of the update sequence on a quadratic objective and control the error caused by Hessian variation on a general objective. This error determines the choice [MATH] for small [MATH]. We show that gradient descent with our stepsize rule finds an [MATH]-stationary point within [MATH] gradient evaluations, matching the optimal gradient-complexity guarantee.
tldr: The paper introduces a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent that achieves optimal O(ε^{-7/4}) gradient complexity for finding ε-stationary points of nonconvex functions.
motivation: Fixed stepsizes in classical gradient descent analysis only guarantee limited decrease per update, leaving a gap to the optimal gradient-complexity bound for nonconvex optimization.
method: The authors use sequences of O(ε^{-1/2}) updates with total stepsize of order ε^{1/2}, prove a weighted descent inequality on quadratic objectives via prefix sums, and bound the error from Hessian variation for general objectives.
result: Gradient descent with the proposed stepsize rule finds an ε-stationary point within O(ε^{-7/4}) gradient evaluations, matching the optimal complexity guarantee.
conclusion: A simple deterministic stepsize schedule suffices to attain optimal convergence rates in nonconvex optimization, with the Hessian-variation error dictating the stepsize scaling.

title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games In Hilbert Spaces And Applications
authors: De-Xuan Xu Zhen Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, [MATH], tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the [MATH]-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an [MATH]-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.
tldr: The paper studies linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games for heterogeneous agents whose dynamics are infinite-dimensional stochastic evolution equations in Hilbert spaces.
motivation: It extends finite-dimensional graphon mean-field games to Hilbert-space settings with unbounded operators, state/control-dependent diffusion, and indefinite cost parameters, motivated by large-network games and delay investment applications.
method: Using Nash certainty equivalence, the limit game is reduced to an operator-valued Riccati equation and a graphon mean-field game system; solvability is analyzed via spectral decomposition, yielding decentralized strategies for the finite-agent game.
result: The authors characterize a strongly regular Riccati solution through an equivalent verifiable condition, establish sufficient conditions for the limit system, and show that the resulting decentralized strategies form an epsilon-Nash equilibrium under convergence assumptions.
conclusion: The framework provides a Hilbert-space theory for graphon mean-field games and applies it to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

title: Kernel Estimates And Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund Theory In The $(k,a)$-generalized Laguerre Setting
authors: Mingwei Shi, Yongsheng Han, Yu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish heat and Poisson kernel estimates for [MATH] in the [MATH]-generalized Laguerre setting, where [MATH] is the Dunkl Laplacian associated with a finite reflection group. The heat kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, and conservative, and satisfies a Gaussian bound in the orbit distance together with polynomial decay in the distance between the transformed coordinates. The Poisson kernel, obtained by subordination, satisfies corresponding size and time-derivative estimates, while [MATH] has integral zero in each variable. Motivated by these estimates, we introduce a class of [MATH]-Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund singular integral operators and show that [MATH]-boundedness implies [MATH]-boundedness for [MATH], together with weak type [MATH] and [MATH]-to-[MATH] estimates. Finally, we establish a [MATH] theorem characterizing the [MATH]-boundedness of such operators by the conditions [MATH], [MATH], and the weak boundedness property.
tldr: The paper develops heat and Poisson kernel estimates in a (k,a)-generalized Laguerre setting associated with the Dunkl Laplacian and builds a corresponding Calderón-Zygmund singular integral theory.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical harmonic analysis tools, particularly Calderón-Zygmund theory, to a generalized Laguerre setting involving Dunkl operators and finite reflection groups.
method: They establish Gaussian and polynomial-decay bounds for heat kernels, derive Poisson kernel estimates via subordination, and introduce a class of (k,a)-Calderón-Zygmund singular integral operators.
result: The main results include L^p boundedness, weak-type estimates, and a T1-type theorem characterizing boundedness of these operators under cancellation and weak boundedness conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a functional-analytic framework for singular integrals in the (k,a)-generalized Laguerre setting, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Saddle-focus To Saddle Transition Of 4d Heteroclinic Orbits Resembling Oscillatory And Regularized Shock Waves Of Some Dissipative Boussinesq Systems
authors: Rezwana Razzaque Angana, Brendan Harding, Dimitrios Mitsotakis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.31934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation.
